\title{Dyck words and binary trees}

\section*{Definitions}
\paragraph{Of nat.} Let \(n\) be a natural number. Then \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Step\mathord{:}of\,Nat}(n) = \operatorname{cond}(\operatorname{Nat\mathord{:}beq}(n,\allowbreak{} 0),\allowbreak{} U,\allowbreak{} D)\).

\paragraph{Cases on.} Let \(\mathit{motive}\) be a function of type \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Step} \to \mathsf{Sort}\). Let \(t\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Step}\). Let \(U\) be an element of \(\mathit{motive}\left(U\right)\). Let \(D\) be an element of \(\mathit{motive}\left(D\right)\). Then \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Step\mathord{:}cases\,On}(t,\allowbreak{} U,\allowbreak{} D) = \operatorname{Dyck\,Step\mathord{:}rec}(U,\allowbreak{} D,\allowbreak{} t)\).

\paragraph{To ctor idx.} Let \(x\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Step}\). Then \(\operatorname{to\,Ctor\,Idx}\left(x\right) = \operatorname{Dyck\,Step\mathord{:}cases\,On}\left(x, 0, 1\right)\).

\paragraph{Inst zero dyck word.} \par\noindent\refstepcounter{definingequation}\label{defeq:1}\paperlineanchor{defeq:1}\textup{(\paperlink{defeq:1}{D1})} \(\operatorname{inst\,Zero\,Dyck\,Word} = \operatorname{Zero\mathord{:}mk}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle\,\rangle))\).

\paragraph{Nest.} \par\noindent\refstepcounter{definingequation}\label{defeq:2}\paperlineanchor{defeq:2}\textup{(\paperlink{defeq:2}{D2})} Let \(p\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word}\). Then \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}nest}(p) = \operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{to\,List}(p) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle)\).

\paragraph{Inst decidable equals dyck step.} \par\noindent\refstepcounter{definingequation}\label{defeq:3}\paperlineanchor{defeq:3}\textup{(\paperlink{defeq:3}{D3})} Let \(x\) and \(y\) be elements of \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Step}\). Given a proof \(h\) of \(\operatorname{to\,Ctor\,Idx}\left(x\right) = \operatorname{to\,Ctor\,Idx}\left(y\right)\), \(\operatorname{inst\,Decidable\,Eq\,Dyck\,Step}\left(x, y\right) = \operatorname{is\,True}\). Given a proof \(h\) of \(\neg \left(\operatorname{to\,Ctor\,Idx}\left(x\right) = \operatorname{to\,Ctor\,Idx}\left(y\right)\right)\), \(\operatorname{inst\,Decidable\,Eq\,Dyck\,Step}\left(x, y\right) = \operatorname{is\,False}\).

\paragraph{Is nested.} \par\noindent\refstepcounter{definingequation}\label{defeq:4}\paperlineanchor{defeq:4}\textup{(\paperlink{defeq:4}{D4})} Let \(p\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word}\). Then \(\operatorname{Is\,Nested}(p) = (p \ne 0 \land (\forall i\, :\, \mathbb{N},\; 0 < i \implies i < \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) \implies \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p))) < \operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)))))\).

\paragraph{Denest.} \par\noindent\refstepcounter{definingequation}\label{defeq:5}\paperlineanchor{defeq:5}\textup{(\paperlink{defeq:5}{D5})} Let \(p\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word}\). Let \(\mathit{hn}\) be a proof of \(\operatorname{Is\,Nested}\left(p\right)\). Then \(\operatorname{denest}(p) = \operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\operatorname{tail}(\operatorname{drop\,Last}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))))\).

\paragraph{Semilength.} \par\noindent\refstepcounter{definingequation}\label{defeq:6}\paperlineanchor{defeq:6}\textup{(\paperlink{defeq:6}{D6})} Let \(p\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word}\). Then \(\operatorname{semilength}(p) = \operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p))\).

\paragraph{Inst sum dyck word.} \par\noindent\refstepcounter{definingequation}\label{defeq:7}\paperlineanchor{defeq:7}\textup{(\paperlink{defeq:7}{D7})} \(\operatorname{inst\,Add\,Dyck\,Word} = \operatorname{Add\mathord{:}mk}(p \mapsto q \mapsto \operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p) \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{to\,List}(q)))\).

\paragraph{First return.} \par\noindent\refstepcounter{definingequation}\label{defeq:8}\paperlineanchor{defeq:8}\textup{(\paperlink{defeq:8}{D8})} Let \(p\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word}\). Then \(\operatorname{first\,Return}(p) = \operatorname{find\,Idx}(i \mapsto \operatorname{decide}(\operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i + 1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p))) = \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i + 1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)))),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{range}(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))))\).

\paragraph{Equality test (Dyck word).} \par\noindent\refstepcounter{definingequation}\label{defeq:9}\paperlineanchor{defeq:9}\textup{(\paperlink{defeq:9}{D9})} Compare the underlying lists. Two records are equal exactly when these values agree.

\paragraph{Take.} \par\noindent\refstepcounter{definingequation}\label{defeq:10}\paperlineanchor{defeq:10}\textup{(\paperlink{defeq:10}{D10})} Let \(p\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word}\). Let \(i\) be a natural number. Let \(\mathit{hi}\) be a proof of \(\operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p))) = \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)))\). Then \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}take}(p,\allowbreak{} i) = \operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)))\).

\paragraph{Inside part.} \par\noindent\refstepcounter{definingequation}\label{defeq:11}\paperlineanchor{defeq:11}\textup{(\paperlink{defeq:11}{D11})} Let \(p\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word}\). If \(p = 0\), then \(\operatorname{inside\,Part}\left(p\right) = 0\). Given a proof \(h\) of \(\neg \left(p = 0\right)\), \(\operatorname{inside\,Part}(p) = \operatorname{denest}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}take}(p,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{first\,Return}(p) + 1))\).

\paragraph{Drop.} \par\noindent\refstepcounter{definingequation}\label{defeq:12}\paperlineanchor{defeq:12}\textup{(\paperlink{defeq:12}{D12})} Let \(p\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word}\). Let \(i\) be a natural number. Let \(\mathit{hi}\) be a proof of \(\operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p))) = \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)))\). Then \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}drop}(p,\allowbreak{} i) = \operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\operatorname{List\mathord{:}drop}(i,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)))\).

\paragraph{Outside part.} \par\noindent\refstepcounter{definingequation}\label{defeq:13}\paperlineanchor{defeq:13}\textup{(\paperlink{defeq:13}{D13})} Let \(p\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word}\). If \(p = 0\), then \(\operatorname{outside\,Part}\left(p\right) = 0\). Given a proof \(h\) of \(\neg \left(p = 0\right)\), \(\operatorname{outside\,Part}(p) = \operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}drop}(p,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{first\,Return}(p) + 1)\).

\paragraph{Inst preorder.} \par\noindent\refstepcounter{definingequation}\label{defeq:14}\paperlineanchor{defeq:14}\textup{(\paperlink{defeq:14}{D14})} \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}inst\,Preorder} = \operatorname{Preorder\mathord{:}mk}\).

\paragraph{Equiv tree to fun.} \par\noindent\refstepcounter{definingequation}\label{defeq:15}\paperlineanchor{defeq:15}\textup{(\paperlink{defeq:15}{D15})} Let \(p\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word}\). If \(p = 0\), then \(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}\left(p\right) = \operatorname{Tree\mathord{:}nil}\). Otherwise, \(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(p) = \operatorname{node}(\operatorname{unit},\allowbreak{} \operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(\operatorname{inside\,Part}(p)),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(\operatorname{outside\,Part}(p)))\).

\paragraph{Equiv tree inv fun.} \par\noindent\refstepcounter{definingequation}\label{defeq:16}\paperlineanchor{defeq:16}\textup{(\paperlink{defeq:16}{D16})} \(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,Inv\,Fun}\left(\operatorname{Tree\mathord{:}nil}\right) = 0\).
\par\noindent\refstepcounter{definingequation}\label{defeq:17}\paperlineanchor{defeq:17}\textup{(\paperlink{defeq:17}{D17})} Let \(a\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Unit}\). Let \(l\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Tree}\left(\operatorname{Unit}\right)\). Let \(r\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Tree}\left(\operatorname{Unit}\right)\). Then \(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,Inv\,Fun}(\operatorname{node}(a,\allowbreak{} l,\allowbreak{} r)) = \operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}nest}(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,Inv\,Fun}(l)) + \operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,Inv\,Fun}(r)\).

\paragraph{Equiv tree.} \par\noindent\refstepcounter{definingequation}\label{defeq:18}\paperlineanchor{defeq:18}\textup{(\paperlink{defeq:18}{D18})} The equivalence \(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree}\) goes from \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word}\) to \(\operatorname{Tree}\left(\operatorname{Unit}\right)\). Its forward map is \(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}\). Its inverse map is \(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,Inv\,Fun}\).

\paragraph{Equiv trees of num nodes equals.} \par\noindent\refstepcounter{definingequation}\label{defeq:19}\paperlineanchor{defeq:19}\textup{(\paperlink{defeq:19}{D19})} Let \(n\) be a natural number. The equivalence \(\operatorname{equiv\,Trees\,Of\,Num\,Nodes\,Eq}\left(n\right)\) goes from \(\{p\in \operatorname{Dyck\,Word} \mid \operatorname{semilength}\left(p\right) = n\}\) to \(\operatorname{trees\,Of\,Num\,Nodes\,Eq}\left(n\right)\). Its forward map is \(x \mapsto \operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}equiv\,Trees\,Of\,Num\,Nodes\,Eq\mathord{:}match\,1}(n,\allowbreak{} x_{1} \mapsto \operatorname{trees\,Of\,Num\,Nodes\,Eq}(n),\allowbreak{} x,\allowbreak{} p \mapsto \mathit{property} \mapsto (\operatorname{equiv\,Tree}(p)\, :\, \operatorname{trees\,Of\,Num\,Nodes\,Eq}(n)))\). Its inverse map is \(x \mapsto \operatorname{match\,2}(n,\allowbreak{} x_{1} \mapsto \{p\in \operatorname{Dyck\,Word} \mid \operatorname{semilength}(p) = n\},\allowbreak{} x,\allowbreak{} \mathit{tr} \mapsto \mathit{property} \mapsto ((\operatorname{equiv\,Tree}^{-1})(\mathit{tr})\, :\, \{p\in \operatorname{Dyck\,Word} \mid \operatorname{semilength}(p) = n\}))\).

\paragraph{Inst fintype subtype equals nat semilength.} \par\noindent\refstepcounter{definingequation}\label{defeq:20}\paperlineanchor{defeq:20}\textup{(\paperlink{defeq:20}{D20})} Let \(n\) be a natural number. Then \(\operatorname{inst\,Fintype\,Subtype\,Eq\,Nat\,Semilength} = \operatorname{of\,Equiv}(\operatorname{trees\,Of\,Num\,Nodes\,Eq}(n),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{equiv\,Trees\,Of\,Num\,Nodes\,Eq}(n)^{-1})\).

\subsection*{Prerequisites}
\begin{description}
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4164644c65667443616e63656c4d6f6e6f69642e6164645f65715f7a65726f}\paperlink{premise:4164644c65667443616e63656c4d6f6e6f69642e6164645f65715f7a65726f}{P1.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4164644c65667443616e63656c4d6f6e6f69642e6164645f65715f7a65726f}\textbf{Sum equals zero.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Fix a structure \(\mathit{inst}\) of type \(\operatorname{Add\,Left\,Cancel\,Monoid}\left(\alpha\right)\). Assume \(\operatorname{Add\,Units}\left(\alpha\right)\text{ has at most one element}\). Let \(a\) and \(b\) be elements of \(\alpha\). Then \(a + b = 0 \iff a = 0 \land b = 0\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:436c6173736963616c2e6f725f6966665f6e6f745f696d705f6c656674}\paperlink{premise:436c6173736963616c2e6f725f6966665f6e6f745f696d705f6c656674}{P2.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:436c6173736963616c2e6f725f6966665f6e6f745f696d705f6c656674}\textbf{Or if and only if not imp left.} Let \(a\) and \(b\) be propositions. Then \(a \lor b \iff \neg a \implies b\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:446563696461626c652e6279436f6e74726164696374696f6e}\paperlink{premise:446563696461626c652e6279436f6e74726164696374696f6e}{P3.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:446563696461626c652e6279436f6e74726164696374696f6e}\textbf{By contradiction.} Let \(p\) be a proposition. Assume \(p\) is decidable. Assume \(\neg p \implies \mathrm{False}\). Then \(p\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4479636b537465702e6e6f436f6e667573696f6e}\paperlink{premise:4479636b537465702e6e6f436f6e667573696f6e}{P4.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4479636b537465702e6e6f436f6e667573696f6e}\textbf{No confusion.} Let \(P\) be a proposition. Let \(x\) and \(y\) be elements of \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Step}\). Assume \(x = y\). Then \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Step\mathord{:}no\,Confusion\,Type}\left(P, x, y\right)\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4479636b576f72642e636f756e745f445f6c655f636f756e745f55}\paperlink{premise:4479636b576f72642e636f756e745f445f6c655f636f756e745f55}{P5.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4479636b576f72642e636f756e745f445f6c655f636f756e745f55}\textbf{Count d at most count u.} Let \(\mathit{self}\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word}\). Let \(i\) be a natural number. Then \(\operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(\mathit{self}))) \le \operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(\mathit{self})))\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4479636b576f72642e636f756e745f555f65715f636f756e745f44}\paperlink{premise:4479636b576f72642e636f756e745f555f65715f636f756e745f44}{P6.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4479636b576f72642e636f756e745f555f65715f636f756e745f44}\textbf{Count u equals count d.} Let \(\mathit{self}\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word}\). Then \(\operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(\mathit{self})) = \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(\mathit{self}))\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:45712e6d70725f6e6f74}\paperlink{premise:45712e6d70725f6e6f74}{P7.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:45712e6d70725f6e6f74}\textbf{Mpr not.} Let \(p\) and \(q\) be propositions. Assume \(p = q\). Assume \(\neg q\). Then \(\neg p\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:45712e737562737472}\paperlink{premise:45712e737562737472}{P8.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:45712e737562737472}\textbf{Substr.} Let \(\alpha\) be a sort. Let \(p\) be a function of type \(\alpha \to \mathsf{Prop}\). Let \(a\) and \(b\) be elements of \(\alpha\). Assume \(b = a\). Assume \(p\left(a\right)\). Then \(p\left(b\right)\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:45717569762e636f655f666e5f6d6b}\paperlink{premise:45717569762e636f655f666e5f6d6b}{P9.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:45717569762e636f655f666e5f6d6b}\textbf{Coercion fn mk.} Let \(\alpha\) be a sort. Let \(\beta\) be a sort. Let \(f\) be a function of type \(\alpha \to \beta\). Let \(g\) be a function of type \(\beta \to \alpha\). Let \(l\) be a proof of \(\operatorname{Left\,Inverse}\left(g, f\right)\). Let \(r\) be a proof of \(\operatorname{Right\,Inverse}\left(g, f\right)\). Then \(\operatorname{coe}\left(\operatorname{Equiv\mathord{:}mk}\left(f, g\right)\right) = f\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:46696e747970652e636172645f636f65}\paperlink{premise:46696e747970652e636172645f636f65}{P10.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:46696e747970652e636172645f636f65}\textbf{Cardinality coercion.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Let \(s\) be a finite subset of \(\alpha\). Fix a finite enumeration of \(s\). Then \(\left|s\right| = \left|s\right|\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:46696e747970652e636172645f636f6e677227}\paperlink{premise:46696e747970652e636172645f636f6e677227}{P11.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:46696e747970652e636172645f636f6e677227}\textbf{Cardinality congr'.} Let \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) be types. Fix a finite enumeration of \(\alpha\). Fix a finite enumeration of \(\beta\). Assume \(\alpha = \beta\). Then \(\left|\alpha\right| = \left|\beta\right|\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:46696e747970652e6f6645717569765f63617264}\paperlink{premise:46696e747970652e6f6645717569765f63617264}{P12.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:46696e747970652e6f6645717569765f63617264}\textbf{Of equiv cardinality.} Let \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) be types. Fix a finite enumeration of \(\alpha\). Let \(f\) be a bijection from \(\alpha\) to \(\beta\). Then \(\left|\beta\right| = \left|\alpha\right|\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4966662e6d7072}\paperlink{premise:4966662e6d7072}{P13.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4966662e6d7072}\textbf{Mpr.} Let \(a\) and \(b\) be propositions. Assume \(a \iff b\). Assume \(b\). Then \(a\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4966662e6e65}\paperlink{premise:4966662e6e65}{P14.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4966662e6e65}\textbf{Differs from.} Let \(\alpha\) be a sort. Let \(\beta\) be a sort. Let \(a\) and \(b\) be elements of \(\alpha\). Let \(c\) and \(d\) be elements of \(\beta\). Assume \(a = b \iff c = d\). Then \(a \ne b \iff c \ne d\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:496e742e6164645f6f6e655f6c655f6f665f6c74}\paperlink{premise:496e742e6164645f6f6e655f6c655f6f665f6c74}{P15.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:496e742e6164645f6f6e655f6c655f6f665f6c74}\textbf{Sum one at most of less than.} Let \(a\) and \(b\) be integers. Assume \(a < b\). Then \(a + 1 \le b\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:496e742e6f664e61745f616464}\paperlink{premise:496e742e6f664e61745f616464}{P16.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:496e742e6f664e61745f616464}\textbf{Of nat sum.} Let \(n\) and \(m\) be natural numbers. Then \(n + m = n + m\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:496e742e6f664e61745f6e6f6e6e6567}\paperlink{premise:496e742e6f664e61745f6e6f6e6e6567}{P17.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:496e742e6f664e61745f6e6f6e6e6567}\textbf{Of nat nonnegative.} Let \(n\) be a natural number. Then \(0 \le n\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:496e742e7375625f65715f7a65726f5f6f665f6571}\paperlink{premise:496e742e7375625f65715f7a65726f5f6f665f6571}{P18.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:496e742e7375625f65715f7a65726f5f6f665f6571}\textbf{Difference equals zero of equals.} Let \(a\) and \(b\) be integers. Assume \(a = b\). Then \(a - b = 0\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:496e742e7375625f6e6f6e6e65675f6f665f6c65}\paperlink{premise:496e742e7375625f6e6f6e6e65675f6f665f6c65}{P19.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:496e742e7375625f6e6f6e6e65675f6f665f6c65}\textbf{Difference nonnegative of at most.} Let \(a\) and \(b\) be integers. Assume \(b \le a\). Then \(0 \le a - b\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:497343616e63656c4164642e746f49734c65667443616e63656c416464}\paperlink{premise:497343616e63656c4164642e746f49734c65667443616e63656c416464}{P20.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:497343616e63656c4164642e746f49734c65667443616e63656c416464}\textbf{To is left cancel sum.} Let \(G\) be a type. Let \(\mathit{inst}\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Add}\left(G\right)\). Let \(\mathit{self}\) be a proof of \(\operatorname{Is\,Cancel\,Add}\left(G\right)\). Then \(\operatorname{Is\,Left\,Cancel\,Add}\left(G\right)\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4973456d7074792e666f72616c6c5f696666}\paperlink{premise:4973456d7074792e666f72616c6c5f696666}{P21.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4973456d7074792e666f72616c6c5f696666}\textbf{Forall if and only if.} Let \(\alpha\) be a sort. Assume \(\alpha\text{ is empty}\). Let \(p\) be a function of type \(\alpha \to \mathsf{Prop}\). Then \(\left(\forall a\, :\, \alpha,\; p\left(a\right)\right) \iff \mathrm{True}\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:49734c65667443616e63656c4164642e6164644c6566745265666c6563744c455f6f665f6164644c6566745265666c6563744c54}\paperlink{premise:49734c65667443616e63656c4164642e6164644c6566745265666c6563744c455f6f665f6164644c6566745265666c6563744c54}{P22.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:49734c65667443616e63656c4164642e6164644c6566745265666c6563744c455f6f665f6164644c6566745265666c6563744c54}\textbf{Sum left reflect at most of sum left reflect less than.} Let \(N\) be a type. Fix a structure \(\mathit{inst}\) of type \(\operatorname{Add}\left(N\right)\). Let \(\mathit{inst}_{1}\) be a proof of \(\operatorname{Is\,Left\,Cancel\,Add}\left(N\right)\). Equip \(N\) with a partial order. Let \(\mathit{inst}_{3}\) be a proof of \(\operatorname{Add\,Left\,Reflect\,LT}\left(N\right)\). Then \(\operatorname{Add\,Left\,Reflect\,LE}\left(N\right)\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:49734f7264657265644164644d6f6e6f69642e746f4164644c6566744d6f6e6f}\paperlink{premise:49734f7264657265644164644d6f6e6f69642e746f4164644c6566744d6f6e6f}{P23.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:49734f7264657265644164644d6f6e6f69642e746f4164644c6566744d6f6e6f}\textbf{To sum left mono.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Equip \(\alpha\) with a commutative additive monoid structure and a partial order. Assume \(\text{translation preserves order on }\alpha\). Then \(\operatorname{Add\,Left\,Mono}\left(\alpha\right)\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:49734f72646572656443616e63656c4164644d6f6e6f69642e746f497343616e63656c416464}\paperlink{premise:49734f72646572656443616e63656c4164644d6f6e6f69642e746f497343616e63656c416464}{P24.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:49734f72646572656443616e63656c4164644d6f6e6f69642e746f497343616e63656c416464}\textbf{To is cancel sum.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Equip \(\alpha\) with a commutative additive monoid structure and a partial order. Assume \(\text{translation preserves and reflects order on }\alpha\). Then \(\operatorname{Is\,Cancel\,Add}\left(\alpha\right)\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c452e6c652e7472616e73}\paperlink{premise:4c452e6c652e7472616e73}{P25.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c452e6c652e7472616e73}\textbf{Alias.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Equip \(\alpha\) with a preorder. Let \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) be elements of \(\alpha\). Assume \(a \le b\). Assume \(b \le c\). Then \(a \le c\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c542e6c742e6c65}\paperlink{premise:4c542e6c742e6c65}{P26.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c542e6c742e6c65}\textbf{Alias.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Equip \(\alpha\) with a preorder. Let \(a\) and \(b\) be elements of \(\alpha\). Assume \(a < b\). Then \(a \le b\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c542e6c742e6e6527}\paperlink{premise:4c542e6c742e6e6527}{P27.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c542e6c742e6e6527}\textbf{Ne'.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Equip \(\alpha\) with a preorder. Let \(a\) and \(b\) be elements of \(\alpha\). Assume \(a < b\). Then \(b \ne a\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e436f6e73747261696e742e616464457175616c6974795f736174}\paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e436f6e73747261696e742e616464457175616c6974795f736174}{P28.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e436f6e73747261696e742e616464457175616c6974795f736174}\textbf{Sum equality sat.} Let \(c\) be an integer. Let \(x\) and \(y\) be elements of \(\operatorname{Coeffs}\). Assume \(c + \operatorname{dot}\left(x, y\right) = 0\). Then \(\operatorname{sat^{\prime}}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Constraint\mathord{:}mk}(\operatorname{some}(-c),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{some}(-c)),\allowbreak{} x,\allowbreak{} y) = \mathrm{true}\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e436f6e73747261696e742e616464496e657175616c6974795f736174}\paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e436f6e73747261696e742e616464496e657175616c6974795f736174}{P29.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e436f6e73747261696e742e616464496e657175616c6974795f736174}\textbf{Sum inequality sat.} Let \(c\) be an integer. Let \(x\) and \(y\) be elements of \(\operatorname{Coeffs}\). Assume \(c + \operatorname{dot}\left(x, y\right) \ge 0\). Then \(\operatorname{sat^{\prime}}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Constraint\mathord{:}mk}(\operatorname{some}(-c),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{none}),\allowbreak{} x,\allowbreak{} y) = \mathrm{true}\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e436f6e73747261696e742e636f6d62696e655f73617427}\paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e436f6e73747261696e742e636f6d62696e655f73617427}{P30.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e436f6e73747261696e742e636f6d62696e655f73617427}\textbf{Combine sat'.} Let \(s\) and \(t\) be elements of \(\operatorname{Constraint}\). Let \(x\) and \(y\) be elements of \(\operatorname{Coeffs}\). Assume \(\operatorname{sat^{\prime}}\left(s, x, y\right) = \mathrm{true}\). Assume \(\operatorname{sat^{\prime}}\left(t, x, y\right) = \mathrm{true}\). Then \(\operatorname{sat^{\prime}}\left(\operatorname{combine}\left(s, t\right), x, y\right) = \mathrm{true}\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e436f6e73747261696e742e6e6f745f736174275f6f665f6973496d706f737369626c65}\paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e436f6e73747261696e742e6e6f745f736174275f6f665f6973496d706f737369626c65}{P31.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e436f6e73747261696e742e6e6f745f736174275f6f665f6973496d706f737369626c65}\textbf{Not sat' of is impossible.} Let \(c\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Constraint}\). Assume \(\operatorname{is\,Impossible}\left(c\right) = \mathrm{true}\). Let \(x\) and \(y\) be elements of \(\operatorname{Coeffs}\). Then \(\neg \left(\operatorname{sat^{\prime}}\left(c, x, y\right) = \mathrm{true}\right)\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e6164645f636f6e6772}\paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e6164645f636f6e6772}{P32.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e6164645f636f6e6772}\textbf{Sum congruence.} Let \(a\), \(b\), \(c\), and \(d\) be integers. Assume \(a = b\). Assume \(c = d\). Then \(a + c = b + d\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e6f664e61745f636f6e6772}\paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e6f664e61745f636f6e6772}{P33.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e6f664e61745f636f6e6772}\textbf{Of nat congruence.} Let \(a\) and \(b\) be natural numbers. Assume \(a = b\). Then \(a = b\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e6f664e61745f6c655f6f665f6c65}\paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e6f664e61745f6c655f6f665f6c65}{P34.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e6f664e61745f6c655f6f665f6c65}\textbf{Of nat at most of at most.} Let \(x\) and \(y\) be natural numbers. Assume \(x \le y\). Then \(x \le y\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e6f664e61745f6c745f6f665f6c74}\paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e6f664e61745f6c745f6f665f6c74}{P35.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e6f664e61745f6c745f6f665f6c74}\textbf{Of nat less than of less than.} Let \(x\) and \(y\) be natural numbers. Assume \(x < y\). Then \(x < y\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e6f664e61745f7375625f646963686f746f6d79}\paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e6f664e61745f7375625f646963686f746f6d79}{P36.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e6f664e61745f7375625f646963686f746f6d79}\textbf{Of nat difference dichotomy.} Let \(a\) and \(b\) be natural numbers. Then \(b \le a \land a - b = a - b \lor a < b \land a - b = 0\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e7375625f636f6e6772}\paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e7375625f636f6e6772}{P37.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e7375625f636f6e6772}\textbf{Difference congruence.} Let \(a\), \(b\), \(c\), and \(d\) be integers. Assume \(a = b\). Assume \(c = d\). Then \(a - c = b - d\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e6164645f6576616c}\paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e6164645f6576616c}{P38.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e6164645f6576616c}\textbf{Sum eval.} Let \(l_{1}\) and \(l_{2}\) be elements of \(\operatorname{Linear\,Combo}\). Let \(v\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Coeffs}\). Then \(\operatorname{eval}(l_{1} + l_{2},\allowbreak{} v) = \operatorname{eval}(l_{1},\allowbreak{} v) + \operatorname{eval}(l_{2},\allowbreak{} v)\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f30}\paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f30}{P39.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f30}\textbf{Coordinate eval 0.} Let \(\mathit{a0}\) be an integer. Let \(t\) be a list of elements of \(\mathbb{Z}\). Then \(\operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{coordinate}(0),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle \mathit{a0}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} t)) = \mathit{a0}\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f31}\paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f31}{P40.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f31}\textbf{Coordinate eval 1.} Let \(\mathit{a0}\) and \(\mathit{a1}\) be integers. Let \(t\) be a list of elements of \(\mathbb{Z}\). Then \(\operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{coordinate}(1),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle \mathit{a0}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{a1}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} t))) = \mathit{a1}\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f32}\paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f32}{P41.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f32}\textbf{Coordinate eval 2.} Let \(\mathit{a0}\), \(\mathit{a1}\), and \(\mathit{a2}\) be integers. Let \(t\) be a list of elements of \(\mathbb{Z}\). Then \(\operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{coordinate}(2),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle \mathit{a0}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{a1}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{a2}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} t)))) = \mathit{a2}\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f33}\paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f33}{P42.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f33}\textbf{Coordinate eval 3.} Let \(\mathit{a0}\), \(\mathit{a1}\), \(\mathit{a2}\), and \(\mathit{a3}\) be integers. Let \(t\) be a list of elements of \(\mathbb{Z}\). Then \(\operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{coordinate}(3),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle \mathit{a0}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{a1}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{a2}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{a3}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} t))))) = \mathit{a3}\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e7375625f6576616c}\paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e7375625f6576616c}{P43.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e7375625f6576616c}\textbf{Difference eval.} Let \(l_{1}\) and \(l_{2}\) be elements of \(\operatorname{Linear\,Combo}\). Let \(v\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Coeffs}\). Then \(\operatorname{eval}(l_{1} - l_{2},\allowbreak{} v) = \operatorname{eval}(l_{1},\allowbreak{} v) - \operatorname{eval}(l_{2},\allowbreak{} v)\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e636f6d626f5f73617427}\paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e636f6d626f5f73617427}{P44.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e636f6d626f5f73617427}\textbf{Combo sat'.} Let \(s\) and \(t\) be elements of \(\operatorname{Constraint}\). Let \(a\) be an integer. Let \(x\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Coeffs}\). Let \(b\) be an integer. Let \(y\) and \(v\) be elements of \(\operatorname{Coeffs}\). Assume \(\operatorname{sat^{\prime}}\left(s, x, v\right) = \mathrm{true}\). Assume \(\operatorname{sat^{\prime}}\left(t, y, v\right) = \mathrm{true}\). Then \(\operatorname{sat^{\prime}}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Constraint\mathord{:}combo}(a,\allowbreak{} s,\allowbreak{} b,\allowbreak{} t),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Coeffs\mathord{:}combo}(a,\allowbreak{} x,\allowbreak{} b,\allowbreak{} y),\allowbreak{} v) = \mathrm{true}\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e746964795f736174}\paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e746964795f736174}{P45.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e746964795f736174}\textbf{Tidy sat.} Let \(s\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Constraint}\). Let \(x\) and \(v\) be elements of \(\operatorname{Coeffs}\). Assume \(\operatorname{sat^{\prime}}\left(s, x, v\right) = \mathrm{true}\). Then \(\operatorname{sat^{\prime}}(\operatorname{tidy\,Constraint}(s,\allowbreak{} x),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{tidy\,Coeffs}(s,\allowbreak{} x),\allowbreak{} v) = \mathrm{true}\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c6973742e4973496e6669782e65715f6f665f6c656e677468}\paperlink{premise:4c6973742e4973496e6669782e65715f6f665f6c656e677468}{P46.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c6973742e4973496e6669782e65715f6f665f6c656e677468}\textbf{Equals of length.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Let \(l_{1}\) and \(l_{2}\) be lists of elements of \(\alpha\). Assume \(\operatorname{Is\,Infix}\left(l_{1}, l_{2}\right)\). Assume \(\operatorname{length}(l_{1}) = \operatorname{length}(l_{2})\). Then \(l_{1} = l_{2}\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c6973742e4973496e6669782e7472616e73}\paperlink{premise:4c6973742e4973496e6669782e7472616e73}{P47.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c6973742e4973496e6669782e7472616e73}\textbf{Trans.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Let \(l_{1}\), \(l_{2}\), and \(l_{3}\) be lists of elements of \(\alpha\). Assume \(\operatorname{Is\,Infix}\left(l_{1}, l_{2}\right)\). Assume \(\operatorname{Is\,Infix}\left(l_{2}, l_{3}\right)\). Then \(\operatorname{Is\,Infix}\left(l_{1}, l_{3}\right)\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c6973742e617070656e645f6173736f63}\paperlink{premise:4c6973742e617070656e645f6173736f63}{P48.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c6973742e617070656e645f6173736f63}\textbf{Append assoc.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Let \(\mathit{as}\), \(\mathit{bs}\), and \(\mathit{cs}\) be lists of elements of \(\alpha\). Then \(\mathit{as} \mathbin{\Vert} \mathit{bs} \mathbin{\Vert} \mathit{cs} = \mathit{as} \mathbin{\Vert} (\mathit{bs} \mathbin{\Vert} \mathit{cs})\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c6973742e617070656e645f6e696c}\paperlink{premise:4c6973742e617070656e645f6e696c}{P49.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c6973742e617070656e645f6e696c}\textbf{Append nil.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Let \(\mathit{as}\) be a list of elements of \(\alpha\). Then \(\mathit{as} \mathbin{\Vert} \langle\,\rangle = \mathit{as}\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c6973742e636f756e745f617070656e64}\paperlink{premise:4c6973742e636f756e745f617070656e64}{P50.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c6973742e636f756e745f617070656e64}\textbf{Count append.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Fix a structure \(\mathit{inst}\) of type \(\operatorname{BEq}\left(\alpha\right)\). Let \(a\) be an element of \(\alpha\). Let \(l_{1}\) and \(l_{2}\) be lists of elements of \(\alpha\). Then \(\operatorname{count}(a,\allowbreak{} l_{1} \mathbin{\Vert} l_{2}) = \operatorname{count}(a,\allowbreak{} l_{1}) + \operatorname{count}(a,\allowbreak{} l_{2})\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c6973742e636f756e745f636f6e73}\paperlink{premise:4c6973742e636f756e745f636f6e73}{P51.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c6973742e636f756e745f636f6e73}\textbf{Count cons.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Fix a structure \(\mathit{inst}\) of type \(\operatorname{BEq}\left(\alpha\right)\). Let \(a\) and \(b\) be elements of \(\alpha\). Let \(l\) be a list of elements of \(\alpha\). Then \(\operatorname{count}(a,\allowbreak{} \langle b\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} l) = \operatorname{count}(a,\allowbreak{} l) + \begin{cases}1 &\text{if } \operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}(b,\allowbreak{} a) = \mathrm{true}\\ 0 &\text{otherwise}\end{cases}\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c6973742e636f756e745f636f6e735f6f665f6e65}\paperlink{premise:4c6973742e636f756e745f636f6e735f6f665f6e65}{P52.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c6973742e636f756e745f636f6e735f6f665f6e65}\textbf{Count cons of differs from.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Fix a structure \(\mathit{inst}\) of type \(\operatorname{BEq}\left(\alpha\right)\). Let \(\mathit{inst}_{1}\) be a proof of \(\operatorname{Lawful\,BEq}\left(\alpha\right)\). Let \(b\) and \(a\) be elements of \(\alpha\). Assume \(b \ne a\). Let \(l\) be a list of elements of \(\alpha\). Then \(\operatorname{count}\left(a, \langle b\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} l\right) = \operatorname{count}\left(a, l\right)\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c6973742e636f756e745f636f6e735f73656c66}\paperlink{premise:4c6973742e636f756e745f636f6e735f73656c66}{P53.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c6973742e636f756e745f636f6e735f73656c66}\textbf{Count cons self.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Fix a structure \(\mathit{inst}\) of type \(\operatorname{BEq}\left(\alpha\right)\). Let \(\mathit{inst}_{1}\) be a proof of \(\operatorname{Lawful\,BEq}\left(\alpha\right)\). Let \(a\) be an element of \(\alpha\). Let \(l\) be a list of elements of \(\alpha\). Then \(\operatorname{count}(a,\allowbreak{} \langle a\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} l) = \operatorname{count}(a,\allowbreak{} l) + 1\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c6973742e636f756e745f65715f6f6e655f6f665f6d656d}\paperlink{premise:4c6973742e636f756e745f65715f6f6e655f6f665f6d656d}{P54.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c6973742e636f756e745f65715f6f6e655f6f665f6d656d}\textbf{Count equals one of membership.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Assume equality on \(\alpha\) is decidable. Let \(a\) be an element of \(\alpha\). Let \(l\) be a list of elements of \(\alpha\). Assume \(l\text{ has no repeated elements}\). Assume \(a \in l\). Then \(\operatorname{count}\left(a, l\right) = 1\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c6973742e636f756e745f73696e676c65746f6e27}\paperlink{premise:4c6973742e636f756e745f73696e676c65746f6e27}{P55.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c6973742e636f756e745f73696e676c65746f6e27}\textbf{Count singleton'.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Assume equality on \(\alpha\) is decidable. Let \(a\) and \(b\) be elements of \(\alpha\). Then \(\operatorname{count}(a,\allowbreak{} \langle b\rangle) = \begin{cases}1 &\text{if } b = a\\ 0 &\text{otherwise}\end{cases}\).

Let \(l\) be a list of elements of \(\alpha\). Let \(h\) be a proof of \(l \ne \langle\,\rangle\). Then \(\operatorname{drop\,Last}(l) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{get\,Last}(l)\rangle = l\).

Let \(l_{1}\) be a list of elements of \(\alpha\). Let \(b\) be an element of \(\alpha\). Then \(\operatorname{drop\,Last}\left(l_{1} \mathbin{\Vert} \langle b\rangle\right) = l_{1}\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c6973742e64726f704c6173745f65715f74616b65}\paperlink{premise:4c6973742e64726f704c6173745f65715f74616b65}{P58.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c6973742e64726f704c6173745f65715f74616b65}\textbf{Drop last equals take.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Let \(l_{1}\) and \(l_{2}\) be lists of elements of \(\alpha\). Let \(i\) be a natural number. Assume \(i \le \operatorname{length}(l_{1})\). Let \(i\) be a natural number. Let \(l\) be a list of elements of \(\alpha\). Assume \(\operatorname{length}(l) \le i\). \item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c6973742e66696e644964785f6571}\paperlink{premise:4c6973742e66696e644964785f6571}{P62.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c6973742e66696e644964785f6571}\textbf{Find idx equals.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Let \(h\) be a proof of \(i < \operatorname{length}(\mathit{xs})\). Then \(\operatorname{find\,Idx}(p,\allowbreak{} \mathit{xs}) = i \iff p(\operatorname{get\,Elem}(\mathit{xs},\allowbreak{} i)) = \mathrm{true} \land (\forall j\, :\, \mathbb{N},\; \forall \mathit{hji}\, :\, j < i,\; p(\operatorname{get\,Elem}(\mathit{xs},\allowbreak{} j)) = \mathrm{false})\).

Let \(p\) be a function of type \(\alpha \to \mathbb{B}\). Let \(\mathit{xs}\) be a list of elements of \(\alpha\). Then \(\operatorname{find\,Idx}\left(p, \mathit{xs}\right) \le \operatorname{length}(\mathit{xs})\).

Then \(\operatorname{length}(\mathit{as} \mathbin{\Vert} \mathit{bs}) = \operatorname{length}(\mathit{as}) + \operatorname{length}(\mathit{bs})\).

Let \(a\) be an element of \(\alpha\). Let \(\mathit{as}\) be a list of elements of \(\alpha\). Then \(\operatorname{length}(\langle a\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \mathit{as}) = \operatorname{length}(\mathit{as}) + 1\).

Let \(p\) be a function of type \(\alpha \to \mathbb{B}\). Let \(l\) be a list of elements of \(\alpha\). \item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c6973742e6c656e6774685f706f735f6f665f6e655f6e696c}\paperlink{premise:4c6973742e6c656e6774685f706f735f6f665f6e655f6e696c}{P73.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c6973742e6c656e6774685f706f735f6f665f6e655f6e696c}\textbf{Alias.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Let \(l\) be a list of elements of \(\alpha\). Assume \(l \ne \langle\,\rangle\). Then \(0 < \operatorname{length}(l)\).

\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4c6973742e6c656e6774685f73696e676c65746f6e}\paperlink{premise:4c6973742e6c656e6774685f73696e676c65746f6e}{P75.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4c6973742e6c656e6774685f73696e676c65746f6e}\textbf{Length singleton.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Let \(b\) be an element of \(\alpha\). Let \(l\) be a list of elements of \(\alpha\). Let \(a\) be an element of \(\alpha\). Then \(a \in \langle b\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} l \iff a = b \lor a \in l\).

Then \(\operatorname{List\mathord{:}no\,Confusion\,Type}\left(P, \mathit{v1}, \mathit{v2}\right)\).

Then \(\langle a\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} l\text{ has no repeated elements} \iff a \notin l \land l\text{ has no repeated elements}\).

Then \(\operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} l) \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}drop}(i,\allowbreak{} l) = l\).

\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f6c745f6571}\paperlink{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f6c745f6571}{P94.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f6c745f6571}\textbf{Not less than equals.} Let \(\beta\) be a type. Equip \(\beta\) with a linear order. Let \(a\) and \(b\) be elements of \(\beta\). Then \(\left(\neg \left(a < b\right)\right) = \left(b \le a\right)\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f6e655f6571}\paperlink{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f6e655f6571}{P95.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4d6174686c69622e5461637469632e507573684e65672e6e6f745f6e655f6571}\textbf{Not differs from equals.} Let \(\alpha\) be a sort. Let \(x\) and \(y\) be elements of \(\alpha\). Then \(\left(\neg \left(x \ne y\right)\right) = \left(x = y\right)\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4e61742e6164645f65715f7a65726f}\paperlink{premise:4e61742e6164645f65715f7a65726f}{P96.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4e61742e6164645f65715f7a65726f}\textbf{Sum equals zero.} Let \(m\) and \(n\) be natural numbers. Then \(m + n = 0 \iff m = 0 \land n = 0\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4e61742e6164645f6c6566745f696e6a}\paperlink{premise:4e61742e6164645f6c6566745f696e6a}{P97.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4e61742e6164645f6c6566745f696e6a}\textbf{Alias.} Let \(m\), \(k\) and \(n\) be natural numbers. Then \(m + n = k + n \iff m = k\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4e61742e6164645f6c745f6164645f6966665f7269676874}\paperlink{premise:4e61742e6164645f6c745f6164645f6966665f7269676874}{P98.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4e61742e6164645f6c745f6164645f6966665f7269676874}\textbf{Sum less than sum if and only if right.} Let \(k\), \(n\) and \(m\) be natural numbers. Then \(n + k < m + k \iff n < m\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4e61742e6164645f72696768745f63616e63656c5f696666}\paperlink{premise:4e61742e6164645f72696768745f63616e63656c5f696666}{P99.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4e61742e6164645f72696768745f63616e63656c5f696666}\textbf{Sum right cancel if and only if.} Let \(m\), \(k\) and \(n\) be natural numbers. Then \(m + n = k + n \iff m = k\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4e61742e696e737443616e6f6e6963616c6c794f726465726564416464}\paperlink{premise:4e61742e696e737443616e6f6e6963616c6c794f726465726564416464}{P100.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4e61742e696e737443616e6f6e6963616c6c794f726465726564416464}\textbf{Inst canonically ordered sum.} \(\operatorname{Canonically\,Ordered\,Add}\left(\mathbb{N}\right)\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4e61742e696e737449734f7264657265644164644d6f6e6f6964}\paperlink{premise:4e61742e696e737449734f7264657265644164644d6f6e6f6964}{P101.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4e61742e696e737449734f7264657265644164644d6f6e6f6964}\textbf{Inst is ordered sum monoid.} \(\text{translation preserves order on }\mathbb{N}\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4e61742e696e737449734f72646572656443616e63656c4164644d6f6e6f6964}\paperlink{premise:4e61742e696e737449734f72646572656443616e63656c4164644d6f6e6f6964}{P102.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4e61742e696e737449734f72646572656443616e63656c4164644d6f6e6f6964}\textbf{Inst is ordered cancel sum monoid.} \(\text{translation preserves and reflects order on }\mathbb{N}\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4e61742e696e73744e655a65726f53756363}\paperlink{premise:4e61742e696e73744e655a65726f53756363}{P103.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4e61742e696e73744e655a65726f53756363}\textbf{Inst differs from zero successor.} Let \(n\) be a natural number. Then \(\operatorname{Ne\,Zero}\left(n + 1\right)\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4e61742e696e73744f726465726564537562}\paperlink{premise:4e61742e696e73744f726465726564537562}{P104.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4e61742e696e73744f726465726564537562}\textbf{Inst ordered difference.} \(\operatorname{Ordered\,Sub}\left(\mathbb{N}\right)\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4e61742e6c655f6f665f6e6f745f6c74}\paperlink{premise:4e61742e6c655f6f665f6e6f745f6c74}{P105.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4e61742e6c655f6f665f6e6f745f6c74}\textbf{At most of not less than.} Let \(a\) and \(b\) be natural numbers. Assume \(\neg \left(a < b\right)\). Then \(b \le a\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4e61742e6c655f7472616e73}\paperlink{premise:4e61742e6c655f7472616e73}{P106.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4e61742e6c655f7472616e73}\textbf{Transitivity of order.} Let \(n\), \(m\) and \(k\) be natural numbers. If \(n \le m\) and \(m \le k\), then \(n \le k\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4e61742e6c655f7a65726f}\paperlink{premise:4e61742e6c655f7a65726f}{P107.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4e61742e6c655f7a65726f}\textbf{At most zero.} Let \(i\) be a natural number. Then \(i \le 0 \iff i = 0\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4e61742e6c745f6164645f6f6e65}\paperlink{premise:4e61742e6c745f6164645f6f6e65}{P108.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4e61742e6c745f6164645f6f6e65}\textbf{Less than sum one.} Let \(n\) be a natural number. Then \(n < n + 1\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4e61742e6c745f6164645f6f6e655f696666}\paperlink{premise:4e61742e6c745f6164645f6f6e655f696666}{P109.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4e61742e6c745f6164645f6f6e655f696666}\textbf{Less than sum one if and only if.} Let \(m\) and \(n\) be natural numbers. Then \(m < n + 1 \iff m \le n\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4e61742e6c745f6164645f7269676874}\paperlink{premise:4e61742e6c745f6164645f7269676874}{P110.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4e61742e6c745f6164645f7269676874}\textbf{Less than sum right.} Let \(a\), \(b\) and \(c\) be natural numbers. If \(a < b\), then \(a < b + c\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4e61742e6c745f6f665f6e6f745f6c65}\paperlink{premise:4e61742e6c745f6f665f6e6f745f6c65}{P111.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4e61742e6c745f6f665f6e6f745f6c65}\textbf{Less than of not at most.} Let \(a\) and \(b\) be natural numbers. Assume \(\neg \left(a \le b\right)\). Then \(b < a\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4e61742e6c745f6f725f67745f6f665f6e65}\paperlink{premise:4e61742e6c745f6f725f67745f6f665f6e65}{P112.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4e61742e6c745f6f725f67745f6f665f6e65}\textbf{Less than or greater than of differs from.} Let \(a\) and \(b\) be natural numbers. Assume \(a \ne b\). Then \(a < b \lor a > b\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4e61742e6c745f7472616e73}\paperlink{premise:4e61742e6c745f7472616e73}{P113.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4e61742e6c745f7472616e73}\textbf{Less than trans.} Let \(n\), \(m\) and \(k\) be natural numbers. If \(n < m\) and \(m < k\), then \(n < k\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4e61742e7375625f6164645f63616e63656c}\paperlink{premise:4e61742e7375625f6164645f63616e63656c}{P114.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4e61742e7375625f6164645f63616e63656c}\textbf{Difference sum cancel.} Let \(n\) and \(m\) be natural numbers. Assume \(m \le n\). Then \(n - m + m = n\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4e652e73796d6d}\paperlink{premise:4e652e73796d6d}{P115.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4e652e73796d6d}\textbf{Symm.} Let \(\alpha\) be a sort. Let \(a\) and \(b\) be elements of \(\alpha\). Assume \(a \ne b\). Then \(b \ne a\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4f722e7265736f6c76655f6c656674}\paperlink{premise:4f722e7265736f6c76655f6c656674}{P116.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4f722e7265736f6c76655f6c656674}\textbf{Resolve left.} Let \(a\) and \(b\) be propositions. Assume \(a \lor b\). Assume \(\neg a\). Then \(b\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:4f722e7265736f6c76655f7269676874}\paperlink{premise:4f722e7265736f6c76655f7269676874}{P117.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:4f722e7265736f6c76655f7269676874}\textbf{Resolve right.} Let \(a\) and \(b\) be propositions. Assume \(a \lor b\). Assume \(\neg b\). Then \(a\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:52656c6174696f6e2e5265666c5472616e7347656e2e73696e676c65}\paperlink{premise:52656c6174696f6e2e5265666c5472616e7347656e2e73696e676c65}{P118.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:52656c6174696f6e2e5265666c5472616e7347656e2e73696e676c65}\textbf{Single.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Let \(r\) be a relation from \(\alpha\) to \(\alpha\). Let \(a\) and \(b\) be elements of \(\alpha\). Assume \(r\left(a, b\right)\). Then \(\operatorname{Refl\,Trans\,Gen}\left(r, a, b\right)\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:53756273696e676c65746f6e2e656c696d}\paperlink{premise:53756273696e676c65746f6e2e656c696d}{P119.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:53756273696e676c65746f6e2e656c696d}\textbf{Elim.} Let \(\alpha\) be a sort. Assume \(\alpha\text{ has at most one element}\). Let \(a\) and \(b\) be elements of \(\alpha\). Then \(a = b\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:547265652e74726565734f664e756d4e6f64657345715f636172645f65715f636174616c616e}\paperlink{premise:547265652e74726565734f664e756d4e6f64657345715f636172645f65715f636174616c616e}{P120.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:547265652e74726565734f664e756d4e6f64657345715f636172645f65715f636174616c616e}\textbf{Trees of num nodes equals cardinality equals catalan.} Let \(n\) be a natural number. Then \(\left|\operatorname{trees\,Of\,Num\,Nodes\,Eq}\left(n\right)\right| = \operatorname{catalan}\left(n\right)\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:556e697175652e696e737453756273696e676c65746f6e}\paperlink{premise:556e697175652e696e737453756273696e676c65746f6e}{P121.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:556e697175652e696e737453756273696e676c65746f6e}\textbf{Inst subsingleton.} Let \(\alpha\) be a sort. Fix a structure \(\mathit{inst}\) of type \(\operatorname{Unique}\left(\alpha\right)\). Then \(\alpha\text{ has at most one element}\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:6164645f65715f7a65726f27}\paperlink{premise:6164645f65715f7a65726f27}{P122.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:6164645f65715f7a65726f27}\textbf{Sum equals zero'.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Fix a structure \(\mathit{inst}\) of type \(\operatorname{Add\,Cancel\,Monoid}\left(\alpha\right)\). Assume \(\operatorname{Add\,Units}\left(\alpha\right)\text{ has at most one element}\). Let \(a\) and \(b\) be elements of \(\alpha\). Then \(a + b = 0 \iff a = 0 \land b = 0\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:6164645f72696768745f636f6d6d}\paperlink{premise:6164645f72696768745f636f6d6d}{P123.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:6164645f72696768745f636f6d6d}\textbf{Sum right commutation.} Let \(G\) be a type. Fix a structure \(\mathit{inst}\) of type \(\operatorname{Add\,Comm\,Semigroup}\left(G\right)\). Let \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) be elements of \(G\). Then \(a + b + c = a + c + b\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:6164645f747375625f63616e63656c5f7269676874}\paperlink{premise:6164645f747375625f63616e63656c5f7269676874}{P124.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:6164645f747375625f63616e63656c5f7269676874}\textbf{Sum tsub cancel right.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Equip \(\alpha\) with a partial order. Fix a structure \(\mathit{inst}_{1}\) of type \(\operatorname{Add\,Comm\,Semigroup}\left(\alpha\right)\). Fix a structure \(\mathit{inst}_{2}\) of type \(\operatorname{Sub}\left(\alpha\right)\). Let \(\mathit{inst}_{3}\) be a proof of \(\operatorname{Ordered\,Sub}\left(\alpha\right)\). Let \(\mathit{inst}_{4}\) be a proof of \(\operatorname{Add\,Left\,Reflect\,LE}\left(\alpha\right)\). Let \(a\) and \(b\) be elements of \(\alpha\). Then \(a + b - b = a\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:6164645f7a65726f}\paperlink{premise:6164645f7a65726f}{P125.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:6164645f7a65726f}\textbf{Sum zero.} Let \(M\) be a type. Fix a structure \(\mathit{inst}\) of type \(\operatorname{Add\,Zero\,Class}\left(M\right)\). Let \(a\) be an element of \(M\). Then \(a + 0 = a\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:616e645f66616c7365}\paperlink{premise:616e645f66616c7365}{P126.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:616e645f66616c7365}\textbf{And false.} Let \(p\) be a proposition. Then \(\left(p \land \mathrm{False}\right) = \mathrm{False}\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:616e645f73656c66}\paperlink{premise:616e645f73656c66}{P127.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:616e645f73656c66}\textbf{And self.} Let \(p\) be a proposition. Then \(\left(p \land p\right) = p\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:616e645f74727565}\paperlink{premise:616e645f74727565}{P128.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:616e645f74727565}\textbf{And true.} Let \(p\) be a proposition. Then \(\left(p \land \mathrm{True}\right) = p\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:6265715f6966665f6571}\paperlink{premise:6265715f6966665f6571}{P129.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:6265715f6966665f6571}\textbf{Beq if and only if equals.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Fix a structure \(\mathit{inst}\) of type \(\operatorname{BEq}\left(\alpha\right)\). Let \(\mathit{inst}_{1}\) be a proof of \(\operatorname{Lawful\,BEq}\left(\alpha\right)\). Let \(a\) and \(b\) be elements of \(\alpha\). Then \(\operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}\left(a, b\right) = \mathrm{true} \iff a = b\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:6265715f73656c665f65715f74727565}\paperlink{premise:6265715f73656c665f65715f74727565}{P130.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:6265715f73656c665f65715f74727565}\textbf{Beq self equals true.} Let \(\alpha\) be a type. Fix a structure \(\mathit{inst}\) of type \(\operatorname{BEq}\left(\alpha\right)\). Let \(\mathit{inst}_{1}\) be a proof of \(\operatorname{Lawful\,BEq}\left(\alpha\right)\). Let \(a\) be an element of \(\alpha\). Then \(\operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}\left(a, a\right) = \mathrm{true}\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:636f6e74726176617269616e745f6c745f6f665f636f76617269616e745f6c65}\paperlink{premise:636f6e74726176617269616e745f6c745f6f665f636f76617269616e745f6c65}{P131.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:636f6e74726176617269616e745f6c745f6f665f636f76617269616e745f6c65}\textbf{Contravariant less than of covariant at most.} Let \(N\) be a type. Let \(\mathit{mu}\) be a function of type \(N \to N \to N\). Equip \(N\) with a linear order. Let \(\mathit{inst}_{1}\) be a proof of \(\operatorname{Covariant\,Class}(N,\allowbreak{} N,\allowbreak{} \mathit{mu},\allowbreak{} \mathit{x1} \mapsto \mathit{x2} \mapsto \mathit{x1} \le \mathit{x2})\). Then \(\operatorname{Contravariant\,Class}(N,\allowbreak{} N,\allowbreak{} \mathit{mu},\allowbreak{} \mathit{x1} \mapsto \mathit{x2} \mapsto \mathit{x1} < \mathit{x2})\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:6465636964655f65715f66616c73655f6966665f6e6f74}\paperlink{premise:6465636964655f65715f66616c73655f6966665f6e6f74}{P132.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:6465636964655f65715f66616c73655f6966665f6e6f74}\textbf{Decide equals false if and only if not.} Let \(p\) be a proposition. Let \(x\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Decidable}\left(p\right)\). Then \(\operatorname{decide}\left(p\right) = \mathrm{false} \iff \neg p\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:6465636964655f65715f747275655f6571}\paperlink{premise:6465636964655f65715f747275655f6571}{P133.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:6465636964655f65715f747275655f6571}\textbf{Decide equals true equals.} Let \(p\) be a proposition. Assume \(p\) is decidable. Then \(\left(\operatorname{decide}\left(p\right) = \mathrm{true}\right) = p\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:646974655f636f6e645f65715f66616c7365}\paperlink{premise:646974655f636f6e645f65715f66616c7365}{P134.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:646974655f636f6e645f65715f66616c7365}\textbf{Dite cond equals false.} Let \(\alpha\) be a sort. Let \(c\) be a proposition. Let \(x\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Decidable}\left(c\right)\). Let \(t\) be a function of type \(c \to \alpha\). Let \(e\) be a function of type \(\neg c \to \alpha\). Let \(h\) be a proof of \(c = \mathrm{False}\). Then \(\begin{cases}t(h_{1}) &\text{given } h_{1}\text{ proving } c\\ e(h_{1}) &\text{given } h_{1}\text{ proving } \neg c\end{cases} = e(\operatorname{of\,eq\,false}(h))\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:646974655f636f6e645f65715f74727565}\paperlink{premise:646974655f636f6e645f65715f74727565}{P135.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:646974655f636f6e645f65715f74727565}\textbf{Dite cond equals true.} Let \(\alpha\) be a sort. Let \(c\) be a proposition. Let \(x\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Decidable}\left(c\right)\). Let \(t\) be a function of type \(c \to \alpha\). Let \(e\) be a function of type \(\neg c \to \alpha\). Let \(h\) be a proof of \(c = \mathrm{True}\). Then \(\begin{cases}t(h_{1}) &\text{given } h_{1}\text{ proving } c\\ e(h_{1}) &\text{given } h_{1}\text{ proving } \neg c\end{cases} = t(\operatorname{transport}^{\leftarrow}_{h}(\mathrm{trivial}))\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:646974655f636f6e6772}\paperlink{premise:646974655f636f6e6772}{P136.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:646974655f636f6e6772}\textbf{Dite congruence.} Let \(b\) and \(c\) be propositions. Let \(\alpha\) be a sort. Let \(x\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Decidable}\left(b\right)\). Assume \(c\) is decidable. Let \(x_{1}\) be a function of type \(b \to \alpha\). Let \(u\) be a function of type \(c \to \alpha\). Let \(y\) be a function of type \(\neg b \to \alpha\). Let \(v\) be a function of type \(\neg c \to \alpha\). Let \(h_{1}\) be a proof of \(b = c\). Assume \(\forall h\, :\, c,\; x_{1}\left(\operatorname{transport}^{\leftarrow}_{h_{1}}(h)\right) = u\left(h\right)\). Assume \(\forall h\, :\, \neg c,\; y\left(\operatorname{transport}^{\leftarrow}_{h_{1}}(h)\right) = v\left(h\right)\). Then \(\begin{cases}x_{1}(h) &\text{given } h\text{ proving } b\\ y(h) &\text{given } h\text{ proving } \neg b\end{cases} = \begin{cases}u(h) &\text{given } h\text{ proving } c\\ v(h) &\text{given } h\text{ proving } \neg c\end{cases}\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:65715f66616c7365}\paperlink{premise:65715f66616c7365}{P137.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:65715f66616c7365}\textbf{Equals false.} Let \(p\) be a proposition. Assume \(\neg p\). Then \(p = \mathrm{False}\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:65715f66616c736527}\paperlink{premise:65715f66616c736527}{P138.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:65715f66616c736527}\textbf{Equals false'.} Let \(p\) be a proposition. Assume \(p \implies \mathrm{False}\). Then \(p = \mathrm{False}\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:65715f6f665f686571}\paperlink{premise:65715f6f665f686571}{P139.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:65715f6f665f686571}\textbf{Equals of heq.} Let \(\alpha\) be a sort. Let \(a\) and \(a^{'}\) be elements of \(\alpha\). Assume \(\left(a\, :\, \alpha\right)\text{ is heterogeneously equal to }\left(a^{'}\, :\, \alpha\right)\). Then \(a = a^{'}\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:65715f6f725f6e65}\paperlink{premise:65715f6f725f6e65}{P140.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:65715f6f725f6e65}\textbf{Equals or differs from.} Let \(\alpha\) be a sort. Let \(x\) and \(y\) be elements of \(\alpha\). Then \(x = y \lor x \ne y\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:65715f73656c66}\paperlink{premise:65715f73656c66}{P141.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:65715f73656c66}\textbf{Equals self.} Let \(\alpha\) be a sort. Let \(a\) be an element of \(\alpha\). Then \(\left(a = a\right) = \mathrm{True}\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:66616c73655f616e64}\paperlink{premise:66616c73655f616e64}{P142.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:66616c73655f616e64}\textbf{False and.} Let \(p\) be a proposition. Then \(\left(\mathrm{False} \land p\right) = \mathrm{False}\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:66616c73655f6f72}\paperlink{premise:66616c73655f6f72}{P143.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:66616c73655f6f72}\textbf{False or.} Let \(p\) be a proposition. Then \(\left(\mathrm{False} \lor p\right) = p\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:666f72616c6c5f636f6e6772}\paperlink{premise:666f72616c6c5f636f6e6772}{P144.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:666f72616c6c5f636f6e6772}\textbf{Forall congruence.} Let \(\alpha\) be a sort. Let \(p\) and \(q\) be functions of type \(\alpha \to \mathsf{Prop}\). Assume \(\forall a\, :\, \alpha,\; p\left(a\right) = q\left(a\right)\). Then \((\forall a\, :\, \alpha,\; p(a)) = (\forall a\, :\, \alpha,\; q(a))\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:666f72616c6c5f70726f705f646f6d61696e5f636f6e6772}\paperlink{premise:666f72616c6c5f70726f705f646f6d61696e5f636f6e6772}{P145.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:666f72616c6c5f70726f705f646f6d61696e5f636f6e6772}\textbf{Forall prop domain congruence.} Let \(p_{1}\) and \(p_{2}\) be propositions. Let \(q_{1}\) be a function of type \(p_{1} \to \mathsf{Prop}\). Let \(q_{2}\) be a function of type \(p_{2} \to \mathsf{Prop}\). Let \(h_{1}\) be a proof of \(p_{1} = p_{2}\). Assume \(\forall a\, :\, p_{2},\; q_{1}(\operatorname{transport}^{\leftarrow}_{h_{1}}(a)) = q_{2}(a)\). Then \((\forall a\, :\, p_{1},\; q_{1}(a)) = (\forall a\, :\, p_{2},\; q_{2}(a))\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:66756e657874}\paperlink{premise:66756e657874}{P146.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:66756e657874}\textbf{Function extensionality.} Let \(\alpha\) be a sort. Let \(g\) be a function of type \(\Pi_{x\, :\, \alpha}\, \beta\left(x\right)\). Assume \(\forall x\, :\, \alpha,\; f\left(x\right) = g\left(x\right)\). Then \(f = g\).

Let \(a\) and \(a^{'}\) be elements of \(\alpha\). Assume \(a = a^{'}\). Then \(\left(a\, :\, \alpha\right)\text{ is heterogeneously equal to }\left(a^{'}\, :\, \alpha\right)\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:69665f6e6567}\paperlink{premise:69665f6e6567}{P148.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:69665f6e6567}\textbf{If neg.} Let \(c\) be a proposition. Then \(\begin{cases}t &\text{if } c\\ e &\text{otherwise}\end{cases} = e\).

Then \(\begin{cases}t &\text{if } c\\ e &\text{otherwise}\end{cases} = t\).
\item[\paperlineanchor{premise:6966665f636f6d6d}\paperlink{premise:6966665f636f6d6d}{P150.}] \refstepcounter{paperpremise}\label{premise:6966665f636f6d6d}\textbf{If and only if commutation.} Let \(a\) and \(b\) be propositions. Then \(\left(a \iff b\right) \iff \left(b \iff a\right)\).

Assume \(p\) is decidable. Assume \(\operatorname{decide}\left(p\right) = \mathrm{true}\). Then \(p\).

Fix a structure \(\mathit{inst}\) of type \(\operatorname{Non\,Assoc\,Semiring}\left(\alpha\right)\). Let \(n\) be an element of \(\alpha\). Then \(2 \cdot n = n + n\).
