\section{Results}
\begin{theorem}\label{theorem:1}
Let \(x\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Step}\). Then
\begin{center}
\(\displaystyle \operatorname{Dyck\,Step\mathord{:}of\,Nat}(\operatorname{to\,Ctor\,Idx}(x)) = x.\)
\end{center}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Consider the possible forms of \(x\).
\emph{U case.}
\begin{proofstep}
By definition, we obtain \(U = U\).
\end{proofstep}
\emph{D case.}
\begin{proofstep}
By definition, we obtain \(D = D\).
\end{proofstep}
This proves \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Step\mathord{:}of\,Nat}\left(\operatorname{to\,Ctor\,Idx}\left(x\right)\right) = x\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{theorem:2}
Let \(s\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Step}\). Then \(s = U \lor s = D\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
By definition, we obtain \(s = s\).
Consider the possible forms of \(s\).
\emph{U case.}
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(s = U\).
By \paperlink{premise:436c6173736963616c2e6f725f6966665f6e6f745f696d705f6c656674}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:436c6173736963616c2e6f725f6966665f6e6f745f696d705f6c656674}}, we obtain \(U = U \lor U = D \iff \neg \left(U = U\right) \implies U = D\).
For the required implication, argue as follows.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(\neg \left(U = U\right)\).
By definition, we obtain \(U = U\).
Use the hypothesis \(\neg \left(U = U\right)\).
The assertion contradicts its negation. Hence \(U = D\).
\end{proofstep}
By the reverse implication, we obtain \(U = U \lor U = D\).
Use the hypothesis \(s = U\).
Reversing the equality, we obtain \(U = s\).
Substituting equals, we obtain \(s = U \lor s = D\).
\end{proofstep}
\emph{D case.}
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(s = D\).
By \paperlink{premise:436c6173736963616c2e6f725f6966665f6e6f745f696d705f6c656674}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:436c6173736963616c2e6f725f6966665f6e6f745f696d705f6c656674}}, we obtain \(D = U \lor D = D \iff \neg \left(D = U\right) \implies D = D\).
For the required implication, argue as follows.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(\neg \left(D = U\right)\).
By definition, we obtain \(D = D\).
\end{proofstep}
By the reverse implication, we obtain \(D = U \lor D = D\).
Use the hypothesis \(s = D\).
Reversing the equality, we obtain \(D = s\).
Substituting equals, we obtain \(s = U \lor s = D\).
\end{proofstep}
This proves \(s = U \lor s = D\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{theorem:3}
Let \(x\) and \(y\) be elements of \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word}\). Assume \(\operatorname{to\,List}\left(x\right) = \operatorname{to\,List}\left(y\right)\). Then \(x = y\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Compare the two records field by field. By hypothesis, \(\operatorname{to\,List}\left(x\right) = \operatorname{to\,List}\left(y\right)\). After substitution, the remaining fields prove the same propositions. Any two proofs of the same proposition are equal by proof irrelevance. The records therefore satisfy \(x = y\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{theorem:4}
Let \(x\) and \(y\) be elements of \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word}\). Then \(x = y \iff \operatorname{to\,List}\left(x\right) = \operatorname{to\,List}\left(y\right)\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Consider the following case.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(x = y\).
Use the hypothesis \(x = y\).
For the required implication, argue as follows.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(y = x\).
For the required implication, argue as follows.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(x = x\).
Assume \(\text{the proof of }\left(x = x\right)\text{ agrees under transport with the proof of }\left(x = x\right)\).
By definition, we obtain \(\operatorname{to\,List}\left(x\right) = \operatorname{to\,List}\left(x\right)\).
\end{proofstep}
Use the hypothesis \(y = x\).
Reversing the equality, we obtain \(x = y\).
Use the hypothesis \(x = y\).
Substituting equals, we obtain \(\text{the proof of }(x = y)\text{ agrees under transport with the proof of }(x = x) \implies \operatorname{to\,List}(x) = \operatorname{to\,List}(y)\).
\end{proofstep}
By definition, we obtain \(y = y\).
Use the hypothesis \(x = y\).
By reflexivity, we obtain \(\text{the proof of }\left(x = y\right)\text{ agrees under transport with the proof of }\left(x = y\right)\).
Substituting equals, we obtain \(\operatorname{to\,List}\left(x\right) = \operatorname{to\,List}\left(y\right)\).
\end{proofstep}
Consider the following case.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(\operatorname{to\,List}\left(x\right) = \operatorname{to\,List}\left(y\right)\).
By \paperlink{theorem:3}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:3}}, we obtain \(x = y\).
\end{proofstep}
Together the two implications give the equivalence. Hence \(x = y \iff \operatorname{to\,List}\left(x\right) = \operatorname{to\,List}\left(y\right)\).
\end{proof}

\section{Dyck word}
\begin{lemma}\label{theorem:5}
Let \(p\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word}\). Then \(\operatorname{to\,List}\left(p\right) = \langle\,\rangle \iff p = 0\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
By \paperlink{theorem:4}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:4}}, we have \(p = 0 \iff \operatorname{to\,List}\left(p\right) = \operatorname{to\,List}\left(0\right)\).
Substituting by \paperlink{theorem:4}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:4}} reduces the claim to \(\operatorname{to\,List}(p) = \langle\,\rangle \iff \operatorname{to\,List}(p) = \operatorname{to\,List}(0)\).
By the defining equations, we obtain \(\operatorname{to\,List}(p) = \langle\,\rangle \iff \operatorname{to\,List}(p) = \operatorname{to\,List}(0)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{theorem:6}
Let \(p\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word}\). Then \(\operatorname{to\,List}\left(p\right) \ne \langle\,\rangle \iff p \ne 0\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
By \paperlink{theorem:5}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:5}}, we obtain \(\operatorname{to\,List}\left(p\right) = \langle\,\rangle \iff p = 0\).
By \paperlink{premise:4966662e6e65}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4966662e6e65}} with \(\alpha = \operatorname{List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Step})\) and \(\beta = \operatorname{Dyck\,Word}\), we obtain \(\operatorname{to\,List}\left(p\right) \ne \langle\,\rangle \iff p \ne 0\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{theorem:7}
Let \(p\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word}\). Let \(h\) be a proof of \(\operatorname{to\,List}\left(p\right) \ne \langle\,\rangle\). Then \(\operatorname{head}\left(\operatorname{to\,List}\left(p\right)\right) = U\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Use the hypothesis \(\operatorname{to\,List}\left(p\right) \ne \langle\,\rangle\).
Consider the possible forms of \(p\).
\emph{Mk case.}
\begin{proofstep}
Fix \(\mathit{toList}\) in \(\operatorname{List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Step})\).
Assume \(\operatorname{count}\left(U, \mathit{toList}\right) = \operatorname{count}\left(D, \mathit{toList}\right)\).
Assume \(\forall i\, :\, \mathbb{N},\; \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \mathit{toList})) \le \operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \mathit{toList}))\).
Assume \(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\mathit{toList})) \ne \langle\,\rangle\).
Use the hypothesis \(\operatorname{count}\left(U, \mathit{toList}\right) = \operatorname{count}\left(D, \mathit{toList}\right)\).
Use the hypothesis \(\forall i\, :\, \mathbb{N},\; \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \mathit{toList})) \le \operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \mathit{toList}))\).
Use the hypothesis \(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\mathit{toList})) \ne \langle\,\rangle\).
Consider the possible forms of \(\mathit{toList}\).
\emph{Nil case.}
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(\operatorname{count}\left(U, \langle\,\rangle\right) = \operatorname{count}\left(D, \langle\,\rangle\right)\).
Assume \(\forall i\, :\, \mathbb{N},\; \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle)) \le \operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle))\).
Assume \(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle\,\rangle)) \ne \langle\,\rangle\).
By definition, we obtain \(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle\,\rangle)) = \operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle\,\rangle))\).
Use the hypothesis \(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle\,\rangle)) \ne \langle\,\rangle\).
The assertion contradicts its negation. Hence \(\operatorname{head}(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle\,\rangle))) = U\).
\end{proofstep}
\emph{Cons case.}
\begin{proofstep}
Fix \(s\) in \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Step}\).
Fix \(\mathit{tail}\) in \(\operatorname{List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Step})\).
Assume \(\operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \langle s\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \mathit{tail}) = \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \langle s\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \mathit{tail})\).
Assume \(\forall i\, :\, \mathbb{N},\; \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \langle s\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \mathit{tail})) \le \operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \langle s\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \mathit{tail}))\).
Assume \(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle s\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \mathit{tail})) \ne \langle\,\rangle\).
Consider the following case.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(\neg \left(s = U\right)\).
The substitution uses the following argument.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(D = U\).
Use the hypothesis \(D = U\).
By \paperlink{premise:4479636b537465702e6e6f436f6e667573696f6e}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4479636b537465702e6e6f436f6e667573696f6e}}, we obtain \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Step\mathord{:}no\,Confusion\,Type}\left(\mathrm{False}, D, U\right)\).
\end{proofstep}
Applying the hypothesis \(\forall i\, :\, \mathbb{N},\; \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \langle s\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \mathit{tail})) \le \operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \langle s\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \mathit{tail}))\), we obtain \(\operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle s\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \mathit{tail})) \le \operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle s\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \mathit{tail}))\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:4f722e7265736f6c76655f6c656674}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4f722e7265736f6c76655f6c656674}} (using \(\neg \left(s = U\right)\)), \paperlink{theorem:2}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:2}}, \paperlink{premise:4c6973742e636f756e745f65715f6f6e655f6f665f6d656d}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c6973742e636f756e745f65715f6f6e655f6f665f6d656d}}, \paperlink{premise:4c6973742e6e6f6475705f636f6e73}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c6973742e6e6f6475705f636f6e73}}, \paperlink{premise:65715f66616c7365}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:65715f66616c7365}}, \paperlink{premise:4c6973742e6e6f745f6d656d5f6e696c}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c6973742e6e6f745f6d656d5f6e696c}}, \paperlink{premise:6e6f745f66616c73655f65715f74727565}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6e6f745f66616c73655f65715f74727565}}, \paperlink{premise:4c6973742e6e6f6475705f6e696c}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c6973742e6e6f6475705f6e696c}}, \paperlink{premise:616e645f73656c66}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:616e645f73656c66}}, \paperlink{premise:4c6973742e6d656d5f636f6e73}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c6973742e6d656d5f636f6e73}}, \paperlink{premise:6f725f66616c7365}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6f725f66616c7365}}, \paperlink{premise:4c6973742e636f756e745f636f6e735f6f665f6e65}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c6973742e636f756e745f636f6e735f6f665f6e65}}, \paperlink{premise:696e73744c617766756c424571}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:696e73744c617766756c424571}}, \paperlink{premise:65715f66616c736527}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:65715f66616c736527}}, \paperlink{premise:6e6f6e706f735f6966665f65715f7a65726f}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6e6f6e706f735f6966665f65715f7a65726f}}, \paperlink{premise:4e61742e696e737443616e6f6e6963616c6c794f726465726564416464}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4e61742e696e737443616e6f6e6963616c6c794f726465726564416464}}, \paperlink{premise:6f6e655f6e655f7a65726f}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6f6e655f6e655f7a65726f}}, \paperlink{premise:4e61742e696e73744e655a65726f53756363}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4e61742e696e73744e655a65726f53756363}} and the auxiliary result established above in the preceding result gives \(\mathrm{False}\).
The contradiction rules out this case. Hence \(\mathrm{False}\).
\end{proofstep}
The contrary assumption leads to a contradiction. Hence \(s = U\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:4c6973742e686561645f636f6e73}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c6973742e686561645f636f6e73}} (using \(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle s\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \mathit{tail})) \ne \langle\,\rangle\)) in the preceding result gives \(\operatorname{head}(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle s\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \mathit{tail}))) = U\).
\end{proofstep}
This proves \(\operatorname{head}(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\mathit{toList}))) = U\).
\end{proofstep}
This proves \(\operatorname{head}\left(\operatorname{to\,List}\left(p\right)\right) = U\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{theorem:8}
Let \(p\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word}\). Let \(h\) be a proof of \(\operatorname{to\,List}\left(p\right) \ne \langle\,\rangle\). Then \(\operatorname{get\,Last}\left(\operatorname{to\,List}\left(p\right)\right) = D\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Consider the following case.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(\neg \left(\operatorname{get\,Last}\left(\operatorname{to\,List}\left(p\right)\right) = D\right)\).
By \paperlink{premise:4479636b576f72642e636f756e745f555f65715f636f756e745f44}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4479636b576f72642e636f756e745f555f65715f636f756e745f44}} with \(\mathit{self} = p\), we obtain \(\operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)) = \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p))\).
By \paperlink{premise:4479636b576f72642e636f756e745f445f6c655f636f756e745f55}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4479636b576f72642e636f756e745f445f6c655f636f756e745f55}} with \(\mathit{self} = p\) and \(i = \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}\left(p\right)) - 1\), we obtain \(\operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) - 1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p))) \le \operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) - 1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)))\).
By definition, we obtain \(\operatorname{decide}(\operatorname{is\,Impossible}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Constraint\mathord{:}mk}(\operatorname{some}(1),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{some}(0))) = \mathrm{true}) = \mathrm{true}\).

By \paperlink{premise:496e742e6f664e61745f616464}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:496e742e6f664e61745f616464}} with \(n = \operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) - 1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)))\) and \(m = 1\), we obtain \(\operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) - 1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p))) + 1 = \operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) - 1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p))) + 1\).

By definition, we obtain \(1 = \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle \operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) - 1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)))\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) - 1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)))\rangle))\).
By \paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e6164645f636f6e6772}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e6164645f636f6e6772}}, we obtain \(\operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) - 1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p))) + 1 = \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{coordinate}(0),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle \operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) - 1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)))\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) - 1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)))\rangle)) + \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle \operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) - 1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)))\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) - 1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)))\rangle))\).

Chaining the equalities, we obtain \(\operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) - 1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p))) - \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) - 1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p))) = \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(0,\allowbreak{} \langle 1\rangle) - \operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(0,\allowbreak{} \langle 0\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle 1\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle \operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) - 1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)))\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) - 1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)))\rangle))\).
By \paperlink{premise:6c655f6f665f6c655f6f665f6571}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6c655f6f665f6c655f6f665f6571}} with \(\alpha = \mathbb{Z}\), we obtain \(0 \le \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(0,\allowbreak{} \langle 1\rangle) - \operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(0,\allowbreak{} \langle 0\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle 1\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle \operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) - 1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)))\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) - 1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)))\rangle))\).
By \paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e436f6e73747261696e742e616464496e657175616c6974795f736174}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e436f6e73747261696e742e616464496e657175616c6974795f736174}}, we obtain \(\operatorname{sat^{\prime}}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Constraint\mathord{:}mk}(\operatorname{some}(-0),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{none}),\allowbreak{} \langle 1\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle -1\rangle,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle \operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) - 1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)))\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) - 1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)))\rangle)) = \mathrm{true}\).
By \paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e636f6d626f5f73617427}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e636f6d626f5f73617427}} with \(s = \operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Constraint\mathord{:}mk}(\operatorname{some}(-1),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{some}(-1))\) and \(t = \operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Constraint\mathord{:}mk}(\operatorname{some}(0),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{none})\) and \(a = -1\) and \(x = \langle 1\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle -1\rangle\) and \(b = 1\) and \(y = \langle 1\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle -1\rangle\) and \(v = \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle \operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) - 1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)))\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) - 1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)))\rangle)\), we obtain \(\operatorname{sat^{\prime}}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Constraint\mathord{:}combo}(-1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Constraint\mathord{:}mk}(\operatorname{some}(-1),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{some}(-1)),\allowbreak{} 1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Constraint\mathord{:}mk}(\operatorname{some}(0),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{none})),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Coeffs\mathord{:}combo}(-1,\allowbreak{} \langle 1\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle -1\rangle,\allowbreak{} 1,\allowbreak{} \langle 1\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle -1\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle \operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) - 1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)))\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) - 1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)))\rangle)) = \mathrm{true}\).
By \paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e746964795f736174}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e746964795f736174}}, we obtain \(\operatorname{sat^{\prime}}(\operatorname{tidy\,Constraint}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Constraint\mathord{:}mk}(\operatorname{some}(1),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{none}),\allowbreak{} \langle 0\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle 0\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{tidy\,Coeffs}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Constraint\mathord{:}mk}(\operatorname{some}(1),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{none}),\allowbreak{} \langle 0\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle 0\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle \operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) - 1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)))\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) - 1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)))\rangle)) = \mathrm{true}\).
By \paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e436f6e73747261696e742e6e6f745f736174275f6f665f6973496d706f737369626c65}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e436f6e73747261696e742e6e6f745f736174275f6f665f6973496d706f737369626c65}}, we obtain \(\mathrm{False}\).
\end{proofstep}
The contrary assumption leads to a contradiction. Hence \(\operatorname{get\,Last}\left(\operatorname{to\,List}\left(p\right)\right) = D\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{theorem:9}
Let \(p\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word}\). Assume \(p \ne 0\). Then
\begin{center}
\(\displaystyle \langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{tail}(\operatorname{drop\,Last}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle = \operatorname{to\,List}(p).\)
\end{center}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
By \paperlink{theorem:6}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:6}}, we obtain \(\operatorname{to\,List}\left(p\right) \ne \langle\,\rangle \iff p \ne 0\).
Use the hypothesis \(p \ne 0\).
By the reverse implication, we obtain \(\operatorname{to\,List}\left(p\right) \ne \langle\,\rangle\).
Use the hypothesis \(p \ne 0\).
Use the previously proved fact \(\operatorname{to\,List}\left(p\right) \ne \langle\,\rangle\).
Consider the possible forms of \(p\).
\emph{Mk case.}
\begin{proofstep}
Fix \(\mathit{toList}\) in \(\operatorname{List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Step})\).
Assume \(\operatorname{count}\left(U, \mathit{toList}\right) = \operatorname{count}\left(D, \mathit{toList}\right)\).
Assume \(\forall i\, :\, \mathbb{N},\; \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \mathit{toList})) \le \operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \mathit{toList}))\).
Assume \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}\left(\mathit{toList}\right) \ne 0\).
Assume \(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\mathit{toList})) \ne \langle\,\rangle\).
Use the hypothesis \(\operatorname{count}\left(U, \mathit{toList}\right) = \operatorname{count}\left(D, \mathit{toList}\right)\).
Use the hypothesis \(\forall i\, :\, \mathbb{N},\; \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \mathit{toList})) \le \operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \mathit{toList}))\).
Use the hypothesis \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}\left(\mathit{toList}\right) \ne 0\).
Use the hypothesis \(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\mathit{toList})) \ne \langle\,\rangle\).
Consider the possible forms of \(\mathit{toList}\).
\emph{Nil case.}
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(\operatorname{count}\left(U, \langle\,\rangle\right) = \operatorname{count}\left(D, \langle\,\rangle\right)\).
Assume \(\forall i\, :\, \mathbb{N},\; \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle)) \le \operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle))\).
Assume \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}\left(\langle\,\rangle\right) \ne 0\).
Assume \(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle\,\rangle)) \ne \langle\,\rangle\).
By definition, we obtain \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle\,\rangle) = \operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle\,\rangle)\).
Use the hypothesis \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}\left(\langle\,\rangle\right) \ne 0\).
The assertion contradicts its negation. Hence \(\operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{drop\,Last}(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle\,\rangle)))) = \langle \operatorname{head}(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle\,\rangle)))\rangle\).
\end{proofstep}
\emph{Cons case.}
\begin{proofstep}
Fix \(s\) in \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Step}\).
Fix \(\mathit{tail}\) in \(\operatorname{List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Step})\).
Assume \(\operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \langle s\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \mathit{tail}) = \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \langle s\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \mathit{tail})\).
Assume \(\forall i\, :\, \mathbb{N},\; \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \langle s\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \mathit{tail})) \le \operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \langle s\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \mathit{tail}))\).
Assume \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}\left(\langle s\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \mathit{tail}\right) \ne 0\).
Assume \(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle s\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \mathit{tail})) \ne \langle\,\rangle\).
Use the hypothesis \(\operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \langle s\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \mathit{tail}) = \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \langle s\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \mathit{tail})\).
Use the hypothesis \(\forall i\, :\, \mathbb{N},\; \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \langle s\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \mathit{tail})) \le \operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \langle s\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \mathit{tail}))\).
Use the hypothesis \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}\left(\langle s\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \mathit{tail}\right) \ne 0\).
Use the hypothesis \(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle s\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \mathit{tail})) \ne \langle\,\rangle\).
Consider the possible forms of \(\mathit{tail}\).
\emph{Nil case.}
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(\operatorname{count}\left(U, \langle s\rangle\right) = \operatorname{count}\left(D, \langle s\rangle\right)\).
Assume \(\forall i\, :\, \mathbb{N},\; \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \langle s\rangle)) \le \operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \langle s\rangle))\).
Assume \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}\left(\langle s\rangle\right) \ne 0\).
Assume \(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle s\rangle)) \ne \langle\,\rangle\).
By definition, we obtain \(s = s\).
Consider the possible forms of \(s\).
\emph{U case.}
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(s = U\).
For the required implication, argue as follows.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(\operatorname{count}\left(U, \langle U\rangle\right) = \operatorname{count}\left(D, \langle U\rangle\right)\).
Assume \(\forall i\, :\, \mathbb{N},\; \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \langle U\rangle)) \le \operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \langle U\rangle))\).
Assume \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}\left(\langle U\rangle\right) \ne 0\).
Assume \(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle U\rangle)) \ne \langle\,\rangle\).

\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(U = D\).
Use the hypothesis \(U = D\).
By \paperlink{premise:4479636b537465702e6e6f436f6e667573696f6e}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4479636b537465702e6e6f436f6e667573696f6e}}, we obtain \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Step\mathord{:}no\,Confusion\,Type}\left(\mathrm{False}, U, D\right)\).

The contradiction rules out this case. Hence \(\operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{drop\,Last}(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle U\rangle)))) = \langle \operatorname{head}(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle U\rangle)))\rangle\).
\end{proofstep}
Use the hypothesis \(s = U\).
Reversing the equality, we obtain \(U = s\).
Use the hypothesis \(\operatorname{count}\left(U, \langle s\rangle\right) = \operatorname{count}\left(D, \langle s\rangle\right)\).
Use the hypothesis \(\forall i\, :\, \mathbb{N},\; \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \langle s\rangle)) \le \operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \langle s\rangle))\).
Use the hypothesis \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}\left(\langle s\rangle\right) \ne 0\).
Use the hypothesis \(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle s\rangle)) \ne \langle\,\rangle\).
Substituting equals, we obtain \(\operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{drop\,Last}(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle s\rangle)))) = \langle \operatorname{head}(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle s\rangle)))\rangle\).

\emph{D case.}
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(s = D\).
For the required implication, argue as follows.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(\operatorname{count}\left(U, \langle D\rangle\right) = \operatorname{count}\left(D, \langle D\rangle\right)\).
Assume \(\forall i\, :\, \mathbb{N},\; \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \langle D\rangle)) \le \operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \langle D\rangle))\).
Assume \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}\left(\langle D\rangle\right) \ne 0\).
Assume \(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle D\rangle)) \ne \langle\,\rangle\).

\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(D = U\).
Use the hypothesis \(D = U\).
By \paperlink{premise:4479636b537465702e6e6f436f6e667573696f6e}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4479636b537465702e6e6f436f6e667573696f6e}}, we obtain \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Step\mathord{:}no\,Confusion\,Type}\left(\mathrm{False}, D, U\right)\).
\end{proofstep}
Use the hypothesis \(\operatorname{count}\left(U, \langle D\rangle\right) = \operatorname{count}\left(D, \langle D\rangle\right)\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:4c6973742e636f756e745f636f6e735f6f665f6e65}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c6973742e636f756e745f636f6e735f6f665f6e65}}, \paperlink{premise:696e73744c617766756c424571}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:696e73744c617766756c424571}}, \paperlink{premise:65715f66616c736527}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:65715f66616c736527}}, \paperlink{premise:6e6f745f66616c73655f65715f74727565}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6e6f745f66616c73655f65715f74727565}}, \paperlink{premise:4c6973742e636f756e745f65715f6f6e655f6f665f6d656d}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c6973742e636f756e745f65715f6f6e655f6f665f6d656d}}, \paperlink{premise:4c6973742e6e6f6475705f636f6e73}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c6973742e6e6f6475705f636f6e73}}, \paperlink{premise:65715f66616c7365}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:65715f66616c7365}}, \paperlink{premise:4c6973742e6e6f745f6d656d5f6e696c}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c6973742e6e6f745f6d656d5f6e696c}}, \paperlink{premise:4c6973742e6e6f6475705f6e696c}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c6973742e6e6f6475705f6e696c}}, \paperlink{premise:616e645f73656c66}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:616e645f73656c66}}, \paperlink{premise:4c6973742e6d656d5f636f6e73}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c6973742e6d656d5f636f6e73}}, \paperlink{premise:6f725f66616c7365}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6f725f66616c7365}}, \paperlink{premise:7a65726f5f6e655f6f6e65}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:7a65726f5f6e655f6f6e65}}, \paperlink{premise:4e61742e696e73744e655a65726f53756363}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4e61742e696e73744e655a65726f53756363}} and the auxiliary result established above in the preceding result gives \(\mathrm{False}\).
The contradiction rules out this case. Hence \(\operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{drop\,Last}(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle D\rangle)))) = \langle \operatorname{head}(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle D\rangle)))\rangle\).
\end{proofstep}
Use the hypothesis \(s = D\).
Reversing the equality, we obtain \(D = s\).
Use the hypothesis \(\operatorname{count}\left(U, \langle s\rangle\right) = \operatorname{count}\left(D, \langle s\rangle\right)\).
Use the hypothesis \(\forall i\, :\, \mathbb{N},\; \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \langle s\rangle)) \le \operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \langle s\rangle))\).
Use the hypothesis \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}\left(\langle s\rangle\right) \ne 0\).
Use the hypothesis \(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle s\rangle)) \ne \langle\,\rangle\).
Substituting equals, we obtain \(\operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{drop\,Last}(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle s\rangle)))) = \langle \operatorname{head}(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle s\rangle)))\rangle\).

\emph{Cons case.}
\begin{proofstep}
Fix \(\mathit{head}\) in \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Step}\).
Fix \(\mathit{tail}_{1}\) in \(\operatorname{List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Step})\).
Assume \(\operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \langle s\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{head}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \mathit{tail}_{1})) = \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \langle s\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{head}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \mathit{tail}_{1}))\).
Assume \(\forall i\, :\, \mathbb{N},\; \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \langle s\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{head}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \mathit{tail}_{1}))) \le \operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \langle s\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{head}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \mathit{tail}_{1})))\).
Assume \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle s\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{head}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \mathit{tail}_{1})) \ne 0\).
Assume \(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle s\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{head}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \mathit{tail}_{1}))) \ne \langle\,\rangle\).
By definition, we obtain \(\operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{drop\,Last}(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle s\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{head}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \mathit{tail}_{1}))))) = \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{drop\,Last}(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle s\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\langle \mathit{head}\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \mathit{tail}_{1})))))\).
\end{proofstep}
This proves \(\operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{drop\,Last}(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle s\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \mathit{tail})))) = \langle \operatorname{head}(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle s\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \mathit{tail})))\rangle\).
\end{proofstep}
This proves \(\operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{drop\,Last}(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\mathit{toList})))) = \langle \operatorname{head}(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\mathit{toList})))\rangle\).
\end{proofstep}
This proves \(\operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{drop\,Last}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))) = \langle \operatorname{head}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))\rangle\).
By definition, we obtain \(\langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{tail}(\operatorname{drop\,Last}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle = \langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{tail}(\operatorname{drop\,Last}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{theorem:7}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:7}} (using \(\operatorname{to\,List}\left(p\right) \ne \langle\,\rangle\)) in the preceding result gives \(\langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{tail}(\operatorname{drop\,Last}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle = \langle \operatorname{head}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{tail}(\operatorname{drop\,Last}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle\).
Rewriting with \(\operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{drop\,Last}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))) = \langle \operatorname{head}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))\rangle\) in the preceding result gives \(\langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{tail}(\operatorname{drop\,Last}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle = \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{drop\,Last}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))) \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{tail}(\operatorname{drop\,Last}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:4c6973742e64726f705f6f6e65}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c6973742e64726f705f6f6e65}} in the preceding result gives \(\langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{tail}(\operatorname{drop\,Last}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle = \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{drop\,Last}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))) \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}drop}(1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{drop\,Last}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{theorem:8}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:8}} (using \(\operatorname{to\,List}\left(p\right) \ne \langle\,\rangle\)) in the preceding result gives \(\langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{tail}(\operatorname{drop\,Last}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle = \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{drop\,Last}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))) \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}drop}(1,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{drop\,Last}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{get\,Last}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))\rangle\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:4c6973742e74616b655f617070656e645f64726f70}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c6973742e74616b655f617070656e645f64726f70}} in the preceding result gives \(\langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{tail}(\operatorname{drop\,Last}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle = \operatorname{drop\,Last}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{get\,Last}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))\rangle\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:4c6973742e64726f704c6173745f617070656e645f6765744c617374}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c6973742e64726f704c6173745f617070656e645f6765744c617374}} (using \(\operatorname{to\,List}\left(p\right) \ne \langle\,\rangle\)) in the preceding result gives \(\langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{tail}(\operatorname{drop\,Last}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle = \operatorname{to\,List}(p)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{theorem:10}
Let \(p\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word}\). Then \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}nest}\left(p\right) \ne 0\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
By \paperlink{theorem:6}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:6}}, we obtain \(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\operatorname{to\,List}(p) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle))) \ne \langle\,\rangle \iff \operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\operatorname{to\,List}(p) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle)) \ne 0\).
By propositional extensionality, we obtain \((\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\operatorname{to\,List}(p) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle))) \ne \langle\,\rangle) = (\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\operatorname{to\,List}(p) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle)) \ne 0)\).
Reversing the equality, we obtain \((\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\operatorname{to\,List}(p) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle)) \ne 0) = (\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\operatorname{to\,List}(p) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle))) \ne \langle\,\rangle)\).
For the required implication, argue as follows.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(\langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\operatorname{to\,List}(p) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle) = \langle\,\rangle\).
Use the hypothesis \(\langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\operatorname{to\,List}(p) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle) = \langle\,\rangle\).
By \paperlink{premise:4c6973742e6e6f436f6e667573696f6e}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c6973742e6e6f436f6e667573696f6e}} with \(\alpha = \operatorname{Dyck\,Step}\), we obtain \(\operatorname{List\mathord{:}no\,Confusion\,Type}(\mathrm{False},\allowbreak{} \langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\operatorname{to\,List}(p) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle),\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle)\).
\end{proofstep}
By \paperlink{premise:65715f66616c736527}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:65715f66616c736527}}, we obtain \((\langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\operatorname{to\,List}(p) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle) = \langle\,\rangle) = \mathrm{False}\).
Applying the same function to equal arguments, we obtain \((\neg (\langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\operatorname{to\,List}(p) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle) = \langle\,\rangle)) = (\neg \mathrm{False})\).
By \paperlink{premise:6e6f745f66616c73655f65715f74727565}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6e6f745f66616c73655f65715f74727565}}, we obtain \(\left(\neg \mathrm{False}\right) = \mathrm{True}\).
Chaining the equalities, we obtain \((\neg (\langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\operatorname{to\,List}(p) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle) = \langle\,\rangle)) = \mathrm{True}\).
Chaining the equalities, we obtain \((\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} (\operatorname{to\,List}(p) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle)) \ne 0) = \mathrm{True}\).
By \paperlink{premise:6f665f65715f74727565}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6f665f65715f74727565}}, we obtain \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}nest}\left(p\right) \ne 0\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{theorem:11}
Let \(p\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word}\). Then
\begin{center}
\(\displaystyle \operatorname{Is\,Nested}\left(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}nest}\left(p\right)\right).\)
\end{center}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
By \paperlink{theorem:10}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:10}}, we obtain \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}nest}\left(p\right) \ne 0\).
For the required implication, argue as follows.
\begin{proofstep}
Fix \(i\) in \(\mathbb{N}\).
Assume \(0 < i\).
Assume \(i < \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}nest}(p)))\).
The substitution uses the following argument.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(\neg \left(i \le \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}\left(p\right)) + 1\right)\).
By definition, we obtain \(\operatorname{decide}(\operatorname{is\,Impossible}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Constraint\mathord{:}mk}(\operatorname{some}(2),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{some}(1))) = \mathrm{true}) = \mathrm{true}\).
By \paperlink{premise:6f665f6465636964655f65715f74727565}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6f665f6465636964655f65715f74727565}}, we obtain \(\operatorname{is\,Impossible}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Constraint\mathord{:}mk}(\operatorname{some}(2),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{some}(1))) = \mathrm{true}\).
Use the hypothesis \(\neg \left(i \le \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}\left(p\right)) + 1\right)\).
By \paperlink{premise:4e61742e6c745f6f665f6e6f745f6c65}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4e61742e6c745f6f665f6e6f745f6c65}}, we obtain \(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}\left(p\right)) + 1 < i\).
By \paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e6f664e61745f6c745f6f665f6c74}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e6f664e61745f6c745f6f665f6c74}}, we obtain \(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}\left(p\right)) + 1 < i\).
By \paperlink{premise:496e742e6164645f6f6e655f6c655f6f665f6c74}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:496e742e6164645f6f6e655f6c655f6f665f6c74}}, we obtain \(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}\left(p\right)) + 1 + 1 \le i\).
By \paperlink{premise:496e742e7375625f6e6f6e6e65675f6f665f6c65}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:496e742e7375625f6e6f6e6e65675f6f665f6c65}}, we obtain \(0 \le i - \left(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}\left(p\right)) + 1 + 1\right)\).
Using \paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f30}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f30}} in reverse gives \(i = \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{coordinate}(0),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle i\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))\rangle))\).
By \paperlink{premise:496e742e6f664e61745f616464}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:496e742e6f664e61745f616464}} with \(n = \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}\left(p\right))\) and \(m = 1\), we obtain \(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) + 1 = \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) + 1\).
Using \paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f31}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e636f6f7264696e6174655f6576616c5f31}} in reverse gives \(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) = \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{coordinate}(1),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle i\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))\rangle))\).
By definition, we obtain \(1 = \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle i\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))\rangle))\).
By \paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e6164645f636f6e6772}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e6164645f636f6e6772}}, we obtain \(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) + 1 = \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{coordinate}(1),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle i\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))\rangle)) + \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle i\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))\rangle))\).
Using \paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e6164645f6576616c}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e6164645f6576616c}} with \(l_{1} = \operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(0,\allowbreak{} \langle 0\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle 1\rangle)\) and \(l_{2} = \operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle)\) and \(v = \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle i\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))\rangle)\) in reverse gives \(\operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(0,\allowbreak{} \langle 0\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle 1\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle i\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))\rangle)) + \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle i\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))\rangle)) = \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(0,\allowbreak{} \langle 0\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle 1\rangle) + \operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle i\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))\rangle))\).
Chaining the equalities, we obtain \(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) + 1 = \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(0,\allowbreak{} \langle 0\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle 1\rangle) + \operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle i\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))\rangle))\).
Chaining the equalities, we obtain \(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) + 1 = \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(0,\allowbreak{} \langle 0\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle 1\rangle) + \operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle i\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))\rangle))\).
By definition, we obtain \(1 = \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle i\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))\rangle))\).
By \paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e6164645f636f6e6772}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e6164645f636f6e6772}}, we obtain \(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) + 1 + 1 = \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(0,\allowbreak{} \langle 0\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle 1\rangle) + \operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle i\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))\rangle)) + \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle i\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))\rangle))\).
Using \paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e6164645f6576616c}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e6164645f6576616c}} with \(l_{1} = \operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle 0\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle 1\rangle)\) and \(l_{2} = \operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle)\) and \(v = \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle i\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))\rangle)\) in reverse gives \(\operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle 0\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle 1\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle i\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))\rangle)) + \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle i\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))\rangle)) = \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle 0\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle 1\rangle) + \operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle i\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))\rangle))\).
Chaining the equalities, we obtain \(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) + 1 + 1 = \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle 0\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle 1\rangle) + \operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle i\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))\rangle))\).
By \paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e7375625f636f6e6772}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e496e742e7375625f636f6e6772}}, we obtain \(i - (\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) + 1 + 1) = \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{coordinate}(0),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle i\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))\rangle)) - \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle 0\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle 1\rangle) + \operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(1,\allowbreak{} \langle\,\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle i\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))\rangle))\).
Using \paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e7375625f6576616c}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e4c696e656172436f6d626f2e7375625f6576616c}} with \(l_{1} = \operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(0,\allowbreak{} \langle 1\rangle)\) and \(l_{2} = \operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(2,\allowbreak{} \langle 0\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle 1\rangle)\) and \(v = \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle i\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))\rangle)\) in reverse gives \(\operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(0,\allowbreak{} \langle 1\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle i\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))\rangle)) - \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(2,\allowbreak{} \langle 0\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle 1\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle i\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))\rangle)) = \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(0,\allowbreak{} \langle 1\rangle) - \operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(2,\allowbreak{} \langle 0\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle 1\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle i\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))\rangle))\).
Chaining the equalities, we obtain \(i - (\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) + 1 + 1) = \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(0,\allowbreak{} \langle 1\rangle) - \operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(2,\allowbreak{} \langle 0\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle 1\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle i\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))\rangle))\).
By \paperlink{premise:6c655f6f665f6c655f6f665f6571}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6c655f6f665f6c655f6f665f6571}} with \(\alpha = \mathbb{Z}\), we obtain \(0 \le \operatorname{eval}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(0,\allowbreak{} \langle 1\rangle) - \operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Linear\,Combo\mathord{:}mk}(2,\allowbreak{} \langle 0\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle 1\rangle),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle i\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))\rangle))\).
By \paperlink{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e436f6e73747261696e742e616464496e657175616c6974795f736174}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c65616e2e4f6d6567612e436f6e73747261696e742e616464496e657175616c6974795f736174}}, we obtain \(\operatorname{sat^{\prime}}(\operatorname{Lean\mathord{:}Omega\mathord{:}Constraint\mathord{:}mk}(\operatorname{some}(-(-2)),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{none}),\allowbreak{} \langle 1\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle -1\rangle,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{of\,List}(\langle i\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \langle \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))\rangle)) = \mathrm{true}\).
Use the hypothesis \(i < \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}nest}(p)))\), which simplifies to \(i < \operatorname{length}(\langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{to\,List}(p) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle)\).

The substitution uses the following argument.

Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:4c6973742e74616b655f617070656e645f6f665f6c655f6c656e677468}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c6973742e74616b655f617070656e645f6f665f6c655f6c656e677468}}, \paperlink{premise:4c6973742e73696e676c65746f6e5f617070656e64}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c6973742e73696e676c65746f6e5f617070656e64}}, \paperlink{premise:4c6973742e6c656e6774685f636f6e73}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c6973742e6c656e6774685f636f6e73}}, \paperlink{premise:446563696461626c652e6279436f6e74726164696374696f6e}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:446563696461626c652e6279436f6e74726164696374696f6e}} and the auxiliary result established above in the preceding result gives \(\operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}nest}(p)))) < \operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(i,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}nest}(p))))\).

\begin{corollary}\label{theorem:12}
Let \(p\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word}\). Let \(\mathit{hn}\) be a proof of \(\operatorname{Is\,Nested}\left(p\right)\). Then
\begin{center}
\(\displaystyle \operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}nest}\left(\operatorname{denest}\left(p\right)\right) = p.\)
\end{center}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
By \paperlink{theorem:4}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:4}}, we obtain \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}nest}(\operatorname{denest}(p)) = p \iff \operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}nest}(\operatorname{denest}(p))) = \operatorname{to\,List}(p)\).
By propositional extensionality, we obtain \((\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}nest}(\operatorname{denest}(p)) = p) = (\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}nest}(\operatorname{denest}(p))) = \operatorname{to\,List}(p))\).
By the preceding argument, we obtain \((\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}nest}(\operatorname{denest}(p)) = p) = (\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}nest}(\operatorname{denest}(p))) = \operatorname{to\,List}(p))\).
Use the hypothesis \(\operatorname{Is\,Nested}\left(p\right)\).
Taking the first conjunct, we obtain \(p \ne 0\).
By \paperlink{theorem:9}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:9}}, we obtain \(\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}nest}(\operatorname{denest}(p))) = \operatorname{to\,List}(p)\).
Substituting along the equality, we obtain \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}nest}\left(\operatorname{denest}\left(p\right)\right) = p\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{theorem:13}
Let \(p\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word}\). Then
\begin{center}
\(\displaystyle \operatorname{denest}\left(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}nest}\left(p\right)\right) = p.\)
\end{center}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
By \paperlink{theorem:4}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:4}}, we obtain \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\operatorname{tail}(\operatorname{drop\,Last}(\langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{to\,List}(p) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle))) = p \iff \operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\operatorname{tail}(\operatorname{drop\,Last}(\langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{to\,List}(p) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle)))) = \operatorname{to\,List}(p)\).
By propositional extensionality, we obtain \((\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\operatorname{tail}(\operatorname{drop\,Last}(\langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{to\,List}(p) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle))) = p) = (\operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\operatorname{tail}(\operatorname{drop\,Last}(\langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{to\,List}(p) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle)))) = \operatorname{to\,List}(p))\).
By the preceding argument, we obtain \((\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\operatorname{tail}(\operatorname{drop\,Last}(\langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{to\,List}(p) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle))) = p) = (\operatorname{tail}(\operatorname{drop\,Last}(\langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{to\,List}(p) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle)) = \operatorname{to\,List}(p))\).
By \paperlink{premise:4c6973742e64726f704c6173745f636f6e636174}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c6973742e64726f704c6173745f636f6e636174}} with \(\alpha = \operatorname{Dyck\,Step}\), we obtain \(\operatorname{drop\,Last}(\langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{to\,List}(p) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle) = \langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)\).
Applying the same function to equal arguments, we obtain \((\operatorname{tail}(\operatorname{drop\,Last}(\langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{to\,List}(p) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle)) = \operatorname{to\,List}(p)) = (\operatorname{tail}(\langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)) = \operatorname{to\,List}(p))\).
By the preceding argument, we obtain \((\operatorname{tail}(\operatorname{drop\,Last}(\langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{to\,List}(p) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle)) = \operatorname{to\,List}(p)) = (\operatorname{tail}(\langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)) = \operatorname{to\,List}(p))\).
By definition, we obtain \(\operatorname{tail}(\langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)) = \operatorname{to\,List}(p)\).
Substituting along the equality, we obtain \(\operatorname{tail}(\operatorname{drop\,Last}(\langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{to\,List}(p) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle)) = \operatorname{to\,List}(p)\).
Substituting along the equality, we obtain \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\operatorname{tail}(\operatorname{drop\,Last}(\langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{to\,List}(p) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle))) = p\).
By the preceding argument, we obtain \(\operatorname{denest}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}mk}(\langle U\rangle \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{to\,List}(p) \mathbin{\Vert} \langle D\rangle)) = p\).
By the preceding argument, we obtain \(\operatorname{denest}\left(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}nest}\left(p\right)\right) = p\).
\end{proof}

\section{Semilength}
\begin{theorem}\label{theorem:14}
\(\operatorname{semilength}\left(0\right) = 0\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By definition, we obtain \(\operatorname{semilength}\left(0\right) = 0\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{theorem:15}
Let \(p\) and \(q\) be elements of \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word}\). Then
\begin{center}
\(\displaystyle \operatorname{semilength}(p + q) = \operatorname{semilength}(p) + \operatorname{semilength}(q).\)
\end{center}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
By \paperlink{premise:4c6973742e636f756e745f617070656e64}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c6973742e636f756e745f617070656e64}} with \(\alpha = \operatorname{Dyck\,Step}\), we obtain \(\operatorname{semilength}(p + q) = \operatorname{semilength}(p) + \operatorname{semilength}(q)\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{theorem:16}
Let \(p\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word}\). Then
\begin{center}
\(\displaystyle \operatorname{semilength}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}nest}(p)) = \operatorname{semilength}(p) + 1.\)
\end{center}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The substitution uses the following argument.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(D = U\).
Use the hypothesis \(D = U\).
By \paperlink{premise:4479636b537465702e6e6f436f6e667573696f6e}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4479636b537465702e6e6f436f6e667573696f6e}}, we obtain \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Step\mathord{:}no\,Confusion\,Type}\left(\mathrm{False}, D, U\right)\).
\end{proofstep}
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:4c6973742e636f756e745f636f6e735f73656c66}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c6973742e636f756e745f636f6e735f73656c66}}, \paperlink{premise:696e73744c617766756c424571}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:696e73744c617766756c424571}}, \paperlink{premise:4c6973742e636f756e745f617070656e64}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c6973742e636f756e745f617070656e64}}, \paperlink{premise:4c6973742e636f756e745f636f6e735f6f665f6e65}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c6973742e636f756e745f636f6e735f6f665f6e65}}, \paperlink{premise:65715f66616c736527}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:65715f66616c736527}}, \paperlink{premise:6e6f745f66616c73655f65715f74727565}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6e6f745f66616c73655f65715f74727565}}, \paperlink{premise:6164645f7a65726f}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6164645f7a65726f}}, \paperlink{premise:4e61742e6164645f6c6566745f696e6a}{\emph{Alias}} (\paperlink{premise:4e61742e6164645f6c6566745f696e6a}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4e61742e6164645f6c6566745f696e6a}}) and the auxiliary result established above gives \(\operatorname{semilength}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}nest}(p)) = \operatorname{semilength}(p) + 1\).
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}\label{theorem:17}
Let \(p\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word}\). Then
\begin{center}
\(\displaystyle \operatorname{semilength}(p) = \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)).\)
\end{center}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By \paperlink{premise:4479636b576f72642e636f756e745f555f65715f636f756e745f44}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4479636b576f72642e636f756e745f555f65715f636f756e745f44}}, we have \(\operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)) = \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p))\).
Substituting by \paperlink{premise:4479636b576f72642e636f756e745f555f65715f636f756e745f44}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4479636b576f72642e636f756e745f555f65715f636f756e745f44}} reduces the claim to \(\operatorname{semilength}(p) = \operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p))\).
By the defining equations, we obtain \(\operatorname{semilength}(p) = \operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p))\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{theorem:18}
Let \(p\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word}\). Then
\begin{center}
\(\displaystyle 2 \cdot \operatorname{semilength}(p) = \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)).\)
\end{center}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The substitution uses the following argument.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(\operatorname{count\,P}(x \mapsto \operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}(x,\allowbreak{} D),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)) = \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p))\).
For the required implication, argue as follows.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(\operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)) = \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p))\).
Assume \(\text{the proof of }(\operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)) = \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)))\text{ agrees under transport with the proof of }(\operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)) = \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)))\).
For the required implication, argue as follows.
\begin{proofstep}
Fix \(x\) in \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Step}\).
By definition, we obtain \(x = x\).
Consider the possible forms of \(x\).
\emph{U case.}
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(x = U\).
By definition, we obtain \(\operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}\left(U, U\right) = \operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}\left(U, U\right)\).
Use the hypothesis \(x = U\).
Reversing the equality, we obtain \(U = x\).
Substituting equals, we obtain \(\operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}(x,\allowbreak{} U) = \operatorname{decide}(\neg (\operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}(x,\allowbreak{} D) = \mathrm{true}))\).
\end{proofstep}
\emph{D case.}
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(x = D\).
By definition, we obtain \(\operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}\left(D, U\right) = \operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}\left(D, U\right)\).
Use the hypothesis \(x = D\).
Reversing the equality, we obtain \(D = x\).
Substituting equals, we obtain \(\operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}(x,\allowbreak{} U) = \operatorname{decide}(\neg (\operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}(x,\allowbreak{} D) = \mathrm{true}))\).
\end{proofstep}
This proves \(\operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}(x,\allowbreak{} U) = \operatorname{decide}(\neg (\operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}(x,\allowbreak{} D) = \mathrm{true}))\).
\end{proofstep}
By function extensionality, we obtain \((x \mapsto \operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}(x,\allowbreak{} U)) = (a \mapsto \operatorname{decide}(\neg (\operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}(a,\allowbreak{} D) = \mathrm{true})))\).
For the required implication, argue as follows.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \((a \mapsto \operatorname{decide}(\neg (\operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}(a,\allowbreak{} D) = \mathrm{true}))) = (x \mapsto \operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}(x,\allowbreak{} U))\).
For the required implication, argue as follows.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \((x \mapsto \operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}(x,\allowbreak{} U)) = (x \mapsto \operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}(x,\allowbreak{} U))\).
Assume \(\text{the proof of }((x \mapsto \operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}(x,\allowbreak{} U)) = (x \mapsto \operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}(x,\allowbreak{} U)))\text{ agrees under transport with the proof of }((x \mapsto \operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}(x,\allowbreak{} U)) = (x \mapsto \operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}(x,\allowbreak{} U)))\).
By reflexivity, we obtain \(\operatorname{count\,P}\left(x \mapsto \operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}\left(x, U\right)\right)\) heterogeneously equal to itself.
\end{proofstep}
Use the hypothesis \((a \mapsto \operatorname{decide}(\neg (\operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}(a,\allowbreak{} D) = \mathrm{true}))) = (x \mapsto \operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}(x,\allowbreak{} U))\).
Reversing the equality, we obtain \((x \mapsto \operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}(x,\allowbreak{} U)) = (a \mapsto \operatorname{decide}(\neg (\operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}(a,\allowbreak{} D) = \mathrm{true})))\).
For the required implication, argue as follows.
\begin{proofstep}

By definition, we obtain \(x = x\).
Consider the possible forms of \(x\).
\emph{U case.}
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(x = U\).
By definition, we obtain \(\operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}\left(U, U\right) = \operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}\left(U, U\right)\).
Use the hypothesis \(x = U\).
Reversing the equality, we obtain \(U = x\).
Substituting equals, we obtain \(\operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}(x,\allowbreak{} U) = \operatorname{decide}(\neg (\operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}(x,\allowbreak{} D) = \mathrm{true}))\).
\end{proofstep}
\emph{D case.}

This proves \(\operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}(x,\allowbreak{} U) = \operatorname{decide}(\neg (\operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}(x,\allowbreak{} D) = \mathrm{true}))\).
\end{proofstep}
By function extensionality, we obtain \((x \mapsto \operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}(x,\allowbreak{} U)) = (a \mapsto \operatorname{decide}(\neg (\operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}(a,\allowbreak{} D) = \mathrm{true})))\).
Substituting equals, we obtain \(\text{the proof of }((x \mapsto \operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}(x,\allowbreak{} U)) = (a \mapsto \operatorname{decide}(\neg (\operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}(a,\allowbreak{} D) = \mathrm{true}))))\text{ agrees under transport with the proof of }((x \mapsto \operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}(x,\allowbreak{} U)) = (x \mapsto \operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}(x,\allowbreak{} U))) \implies (\operatorname{count\,P}(x \mapsto \operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}(x,\allowbreak{} U))\, :\, \operatorname{List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Step}) \to \mathbb{N})\text{ is heterogeneously equal to }(\operatorname{count\,P}(a \mapsto \operatorname{decide}(\neg (\operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}(a,\allowbreak{} D) = \mathrm{true})))\, :\, \operatorname{List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Step}) \to \mathbb{N})\).
\end{proofstep}
By definition, we obtain \((a \mapsto \operatorname{decide}(\neg (\operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}(a,\allowbreak{} D) = \mathrm{true}))) = (a \mapsto \operatorname{decide}(\neg (\operatorname{BEq\mathord{:}beq}(a,\allowbreak{} D) = \mathrm{true})))\).
For the required implication, argue as follows.
\begin{proofstep}

By definition, we obtain \(x = x\).
Consider the possible forms of \(x\).
\emph{U case.}
