\operatorname{to\,List}(p)))\).
Rewriting with \(r^{'} \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{to\,List}\left(p\right) = \operatorname{to\,List}\left(q\right)\) in the preceding result gives \(\operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(q)) - \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(q))) = \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(q)) - \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(q)))\).
Set \(r\) equal to \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}take}(q,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(q)) - \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)))\).
Use the previously proved fact \(\operatorname{count}(U,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(q)) - \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(q))) = \operatorname{count}(D,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(\operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(q)) - \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{to\,List}(q)))\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:4c6973742e74616b655f6c65667427}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c6973742e74616b655f6c65667427}} gives \(r^{'} = \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(\operatorname{length}(r^{'}),\allowbreak{} r^{'} \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{to\,List}(p))\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:6164645f747375625f63616e63656c5f7269676874}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6164645f747375625f63616e63656c5f7269676874}}, \paperlink{premise:4e61742e696e73744f726465726564537562}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4e61742e696e73744f726465726564537562}}, \paperlink{premise:49734c65667443616e63656c4164642e6164644c6566745265666c6563744c455f6f665f6164644c6566745265666c6563744c54}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:49734c65667443616e63656c4164642e6164644c6566745265666c6563744c455f6f665f6164644c6566745265666c6563744c54}}, \paperlink{premise:497343616e63656c4164642e746f49734c65667443616e63656c416464}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:497343616e63656c4164642e746f49734c65667443616e63656c416464}}, \paperlink{premise:49734f72646572656443616e63656c4164644d6f6e6f69642e746f497343616e63656c416464}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:49734f72646572656443616e63656c4164644d6f6e6f69642e746f497343616e63656c416464}}, \paperlink{premise:4e61742e696e737449734f72646572656443616e63656c4164644d6f6e6f6964}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4e61742e696e737449734f72646572656443616e63656c4164644d6f6e6f6964}}, \paperlink{premise:636f6e74726176617269616e745f6c745f6f665f636f76617269616e745f6c65}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:636f6e74726176617269616e745f6c745f6f665f636f76617269616e745f6c65}}, \paperlink{premise:49734f7264657265644164644d6f6e6f69642e746f4164644c6566744d6f6e6f}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:49734f7264657265644164644d6f6e6f69642e746f4164644c6566744d6f6e6f}} and \paperlink{premise:4e61742e696e737449734f7264657265644164644d6f6e6f6964}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4e61742e696e737449734f7264657265644164644d6f6e6f6964}} in the preceding result gives \(r^{'} = \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(\operatorname{length}(r^{'}) + \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)) - \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)),\allowbreak{} r^{'} \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{to\,List}(p))\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:4c6973742e6c656e6774685f617070656e64}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c6973742e6c656e6774685f617070656e64}} in the preceding result gives \(r^{'} = \operatorname{List\mathord{:}take}(\operatorname{length}(r^{'} \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{to\,List}(p)) - \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p)),\allowbreak{} r^{'} \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{to\,List}(p))\).
Rewriting with \(r^{'} \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{to\,List}\left(p\right) = \operatorname{to\,List}\left(q\right)\) in the preceding result gives \(r^{'} = \operatorname{to\,List}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}take}(q,\allowbreak{} \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(q)) - \operatorname{length}(\operatorname{to\,List}(p))))\).
By the preceding argument, we obtain \(r^{'} = \operatorname{to\,List}\left(r\right)\).
Use the hypothesis \(r^{'} \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{to\,List}\left(p\right) = \operatorname{to\,List}\left(q\right)\).
Rewriting with \(r^{'} = \operatorname{to\,List}\left(r\right)\) in the preceding result gives \(\operatorname{to\,List}(r) \mathbin{\Vert} \operatorname{to\,List}(p) = \operatorname{to\,List}(q)\).
By \paperlink{theorem:3}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:3}}, we obtain \(r + p = q\).
By \paperlink{theorem:36}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:36}} with \(r\) in place of its parameter \(p\) and \(p\) in place of its parameter \(q\), we obtain \(p \le r + p\).
Rewriting with \(r + p = q\) in the preceding result gives \(p \le q\).
\end{proofstep}
Using the existential hypothesis, we obtain \(p \le q\).
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}\label{theorem:40}
Let \(p\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word}\). Then \(0 < p \iff p \ne 0\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By \paperlink{theorem:37}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:37}}, we obtain \(0 \le p\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:6e655f6966665f6c745f6966665f6c65}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6e655f6966665f6c745f6966665f6c65}} in the preceding result gives \(0 \ne p \iff 0 < p\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:6966665f636f6d6d}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6966665f636f6d6d}} in the preceding result gives \(0 < p \iff 0 \ne p\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:6e655f636f6d6d}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6e655f636f6d6d}} in the preceding result gives \(0 < p \iff p \ne 0\).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}\label{theorem:41}
\(\operatorname{Monotone}\left(\operatorname{semilength}\right)\).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Fix \(p\) in \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word}\).
Fix \(q\) in \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word}\).
Assume \(p \le q\).
Use the hypothesis \(p \le q\).
Proceed by induction on \(\mathit{pq}\).
\emph{Refl case.}
\begin{proofstep}
By \paperlink{premise:6c655f7265666c}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6c655f7265666c}} with \(\alpha = \mathbb{N}\) and \(a = \operatorname{semilength}\left(p\right)\), we obtain \(\operatorname{semilength}\left(p\right) \le \operatorname{semilength}\left(p\right)\).
\end{proofstep}
\emph{Tail case.}
\begin{proofstep}
Fix \(b\) in \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word}\).
Fix \(c\) in \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word}\).
Assume \(\operatorname{Refl\,Trans\,Gen}(p_{1} \mapsto q_{1} \mapsto p_{1} = \operatorname{inside\,Part}(q_{1}) \lor p_{1} = \operatorname{outside\,Part}(q_{1}),\allowbreak{} p,\allowbreak{} b)\).
Assume \(b = \operatorname{inside\,Part}\left(c\right) \lor b = \operatorname{outside\,Part}\left(c\right)\).
Assume \(\operatorname{semilength}\left(p\right) \le \operatorname{semilength}\left(b\right)\).
By \paperlink{premise:65715f6f725f6e65}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:65715f6f725f6e65}} with \(\alpha = \operatorname{Dyck\,Word}\) and \(x = c\) and \(y = 0\), we obtain \(c = 0 \lor c \ne 0\).
Consider the following case.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(c = 0\).
For the required implication, argue as follows.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(b = \operatorname{inside\,Part}\left(0\right) \lor b = \operatorname{outside\,Part}\left(0\right)\).
Use the hypothesis \(\operatorname{semilength}\left(p\right) \le \operatorname{semilength}\left(b\right)\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:6f725f73656c66}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6f725f73656c66}}, \paperlink{theorem:27}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:27}}, \paperlink{theorem:26}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:26}}, \(b = \operatorname{inside\,Part}\left(0\right) \lor b = \operatorname{outside\,Part}\left(0\right)\) and substitution of equals in the preceding result gives \(\operatorname{semilength}\left(p\right) \le \operatorname{semilength}\left(0\right)\).
\end{proofstep}
Use the hypothesis \(c = 0\).
Reversing the equality, we obtain \(0 = c\).
Use the hypothesis \(b = \operatorname{inside\,Part}\left(c\right) \lor b = \operatorname{outside\,Part}\left(c\right)\).
Substituting equals, we obtain \(\operatorname{semilength}\left(p\right) \le \operatorname{semilength}\left(c\right)\).
\end{proofstep}
Consider the following case.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(c \ne 0\).
Use the hypothesis \(b = \operatorname{inside\,Part}\left(c\right) \lor b = \operatorname{outside\,Part}\left(c\right)\).
Consider the following case.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(b = \operatorname{inside\,Part}\left(c\right)\).
Use the hypothesis \(\operatorname{semilength}\left(p\right) \le \operatorname{semilength}\left(b\right)\).
By \paperlink{theorem:34}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:34}}, we obtain \(\operatorname{semilength}(\operatorname{inside\,Part}(c)) < \operatorname{semilength}(c)\).
Use the hypothesis \(b = \operatorname{inside\,Part}\left(c\right)\).
Reversing the equality, we obtain \(\operatorname{inside\,Part}\left(c\right) = b\).
Substituting equals, we obtain \(\operatorname{semilength}\left(b\right) < \operatorname{semilength}\left(c\right)\).
By \paperlink{premise:4c542e6c742e6c65}{\emph{Alias}} (\paperlink{premise:4c542e6c742e6c65}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c542e6c742e6c65}}) with \(\alpha = \mathbb{N}\), we obtain \(\operatorname{semilength}\left(b\right) \le \operatorname{semilength}\left(c\right)\).
By \paperlink{premise:4c452e6c652e7472616e73}{\emph{Alias}} (\paperlink{premise:4c452e6c652e7472616e73}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c452e6c652e7472616e73}}) with \(\alpha = \mathbb{N}\), we obtain \(\operatorname{semilength}\left(p\right) \le \operatorname{semilength}\left(c\right)\).
\end{proofstep}
Consider the following case.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(b = \operatorname{outside\,Part}\left(c\right)\).
Use the hypothesis \(\operatorname{semilength}\left(p\right) \le \operatorname{semilength}\left(b\right)\).
By \paperlink{theorem:35}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:35}}, we obtain \(\operatorname{semilength}(\operatorname{outside\,Part}(c)) < \operatorname{semilength}(c)\).
Use the hypothesis \(b = \operatorname{outside\,Part}\left(c\right)\).
Reversing the equality, we obtain \(\operatorname{outside\,Part}\left(c\right) = b\).
Substituting equals, we obtain \(\operatorname{semilength}\left(b\right) < \operatorname{semilength}\left(c\right)\).
By \paperlink{premise:4c542e6c742e6c65}{\emph{Alias}} (\paperlink{premise:4c542e6c742e6c65}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4c542e6c742e6c65}}) with \(\alpha = \mathbb{N}\), we obtain \(\operatorname{semilength}\left(b\right) \le \operatorname{semilength}\left(c\right)\).

\section{Tree}
\begin{theorem}[{Semilength equals the node count of the corresponding tree}]\label{theorem:43}
Let \(p\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word}\). Then
\begin{center}
\(\displaystyle \operatorname{semilength}(p) = \operatorname{num\,Nodes}(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree}(p)).\)
\end{center}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
We first prove the following auxiliary lemmas.
\par\smallskip\noindent\paperlineanchor{aux:43:1}\textbf{Auxiliary lemma~43.1.} Let \(p\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word}\). Then \(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,Inv\,Fun}\left(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}\left(p\right)\right) = p\).
\par\noindent\emph{Proof of the auxiliary lemma.} A descending chain would make the natural-number measure \(x \mapsto \operatorname{semilength}\left(x\right)\) strictly decrease at each step, so the relation is well-founded.
Proceed by well-founded induction to prove \(\forall p\, :\, \operatorname{Dyck\,Word},\; \operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,Inv\,Fun}(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(p)) = p\). For an arbitrary element we may assume the claim for each strictly smaller element.
\begin{proofstep}
Fix \(p\) in \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word}\).
Assume as induction hypothesis that \(\forall y\, :\, \operatorname{Dyck\,Word},\; \operatorname{semilength}(y) < \operatorname{semilength}(p) \implies \operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,Inv\,Fun}(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(y)) = y\).
Distinguish whether \(p = 0\) holds.
Consider the following case.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(p = 0\).
Rewriting with \(p = 0\), \paperlink{defeq:15}{defining equation~D\ref{defeq:15}} and \paperlink{premise:646974655f636f6e645f65715f74727565}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:646974655f636f6e645f65715f74727565}} gives \(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,Inv\,Fun}\left(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}\left(p\right)\right) = p\).
\end{proofstep}
Consider the following case.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(\neg \left(p = 0\right)\).
The substitution uses the following argument.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(p = 0\).
By definition, we obtain \(\operatorname{Tree\mathord{:}nil} = \operatorname{Tree\mathord{:}nil}\).
\end{proofstep}
The substitution uses the following argument.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(\neg \left(p = 0\right)\).
By definition, we obtain \(\operatorname{node}(\operatorname{unit},\allowbreak{} \operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(\operatorname{inside\,Part}(p)),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(\operatorname{outside\,Part}(p))) = \operatorname{node}(\operatorname{unit},\allowbreak{} \operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(\operatorname{inside\,Part}(p)),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(\operatorname{outside\,Part}(p)))\).
\end{proofstep}
The substitution uses the following argument.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(\mathrm{False}\).
By definition, we obtain \(\operatorname{Tree\mathord{:}nil} = \operatorname{Tree\mathord{:}nil}\).
\end{proofstep}
The substitution uses the following argument.
\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(\neg \mathrm{False}\).
By definition, we obtain \(\operatorname{node}(\operatorname{unit},\allowbreak{} \operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(\operatorname{inside\,Part}(p)),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(\operatorname{outside\,Part}(p))) = \operatorname{node}(\operatorname{unit},\allowbreak{} \operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(\operatorname{inside\,Part}(p)),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(\operatorname{outside\,Part}(p)))\).
\end{proofstep}
By \paperlink{theorem:34}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:34}}, we obtain \(\operatorname{semilength}(\operatorname{inside\,Part}(p)) < \operatorname{semilength}(p)\).
By \paperlink{theorem:35}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:35}}, we obtain \(\operatorname{semilength}(\operatorname{outside\,Part}(p)) < \operatorname{semilength}(p)\).
Use the previously proved fact \(\operatorname{semilength}(\operatorname{inside\,Part}(p)) < \operatorname{semilength}(p)\).
Apply the induction hypothesis to \(\operatorname{inside\,Part}\left(p\right)\) to obtain \(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,Inv\,Fun}(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(\operatorname{inside\,Part}(p))) = \operatorname{inside\,Part}(p)\).
Use the previously proved fact \(\operatorname{semilength}(\operatorname{outside\,Part}(p)) < \operatorname{semilength}(p)\).
Apply the induction hypothesis to \(\operatorname{outside\,Part}\left(p\right)\) to obtain \(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,Inv\,Fun}(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(\operatorname{outside\,Part}(p))) = \operatorname{outside\,Part}(p)\).
By \paperlink{theorem:32}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:32}}, we obtain \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}nest}(\operatorname{inside\,Part}(p)) + \operatorname{outside\,Part}(p) = p\).
Rewriting with \(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,Inv\,Fun}(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(\operatorname{outside\,Part}(p))) = \operatorname{outside\,Part}(p)\) in the preceding result gives \(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}nest}(\operatorname{inside\,Part}(p)) + \operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,Inv\,Fun}(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(\operatorname{outside\,Part}(p))) = p\).
Rewriting with \(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,Inv\,Fun}(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(\operatorname{inside\,Part}(p))) = \operatorname{inside\,Part}(p)\) in the preceding result gives \(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,Inv\,Fun}(\operatorname{node}(\operatorname{unit},\allowbreak{} \operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(\operatorname{inside\,Part}(p)),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(\operatorname{outside\,Part}(p)))) = p\).
By the preceding argument, we obtain \(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,Inv\,Fun}(\begin{cases}\operatorname{Tree\mathord{:}nil} &\text{if } \mathrm{False}\\ \operatorname{node}(\operatorname{unit},\allowbreak{} \operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(\operatorname{inside\,Part}(p)),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(\operatorname{outside\,Part}(p))) &\text{if } \neg \mathrm{False}\end{cases}) = p\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:646974655f636f6e6772}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:646974655f636f6e6772}}, \paperlink{premise:65715f66616c7365}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:65715f66616c7365}} (using \(\neg \left(p = 0\right)\)) and the two identities established above in the preceding result gives \(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,Inv\,Fun}(\begin{cases}\operatorname{Tree\mathord{:}nil} &\text{if } p = 0\\ \operatorname{node}(\operatorname{unit},\allowbreak{} \operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(\operatorname{inside\,Part}(p)),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(\operatorname{outside\,Part}(p))) &\text{if } \neg (p = 0)\end{cases}) = p\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:646974655f636f6e6772}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:646974655f636f6e6772}} and the two identities established above in the preceding result gives the same displayed equality.
Rewriting with \paperlink{defeq:15}{defining equation~D\ref{defeq:15}} in the preceding result gives \(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,Inv\,Fun}\left(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}\left(p\right)\right) = p\).
\end{proofstep}
The proposition or its negation holds. Hence \(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,Inv\,Fun}\left(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}\left(p\right)\right) = p\).
\end{proofstep}
The induction gives \(\forall p\, :\, \operatorname{Dyck\,Word},\; \operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,Inv\,Fun}(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(p)) = p\).

\par\smallskip\noindent\paperlineanchor{aux:43:2}\textbf{Auxiliary lemma~43.2.} Let \(t\) be an element of \(\operatorname{Tree}\left(\operatorname{Unit}\right)\). Then \(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}\left(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,Inv\,Fun}\left(t\right)\right) = t\).
\par\noindent\emph{Proof of the auxiliary lemma.} Use structural induction on the tree \(t\) to prove \(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}\left(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,Inv\,Fun}\left(t\right)\right) = t\).

Rewriting with \paperlink{defeq:15}{defining equation~D\ref{defeq:15}} and \paperlink{premise:646974655f636f6e645f65715f74727565}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:646974655f636f6e645f65715f74727565}} gives \(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}\left(0\right) = \operatorname{Tree\mathord{:}nil}\).
\par\smallskip\noindent\emph{Node.}\enspace For a node with label \(a\), let \(l\) and \(r\) be the left and right subtrees. Their induction hypotheses give \(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}\left(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,Inv\,Fun}\left(l\right)\right) = l\) and \(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}\left(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,Inv\,Fun}\left(r\right)\right) = r\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{defeq:15}{defining equation~D\ref{defeq:15}}, \paperlink{premise:646974655f636f6e645f65715f66616c7365}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:646974655f636f6e645f65715f66616c7365}}, \paperlink{premise:4164644c65667443616e63656c4d6f6e6f69642e6164645f65715f7a65726f}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:4164644c65667443616e63656c4d6f6e6f69642e6164645f65715f7a65726f}}, \paperlink{premise:556e697175652e696e737453756273696e676c65746f6e}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:556e697175652e696e737453756273696e676c65746f6e}}, \paperlink{premise:65715f66616c7365}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:65715f66616c7365}}, \paperlink{theorem:10}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:10}}, \paperlink{premise:66616c73655f616e64}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:66616c73655f616e64}}, \paperlink{theorem:28}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:28}}, \paperlink{premise:6e6f745f66616c73655f65715f74727565}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:6e6f745f66616c73655f65715f74727565}}, \paperlink{theorem:30}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:30}}, \(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}\left(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,Inv\,Fun}\left(l\right)\right) = l\), \paperlink{theorem:29}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:29}}, \paperlink{theorem:31}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:31}}, \paperlink{premise:7a65726f5f616464}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:7a65726f5f616464}} and \(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}\left(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,Inv\,Fun}\left(r\right)\right) = r\) gives \(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(\operatorname{Dyck\,Word\mathord{:}nest}(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,Inv\,Fun}(l)) + \operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,Inv\,Fun}(r)) = \operatorname{node}(a,\allowbreak{} l,\allowbreak{} r)\).
These cases establish \(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}\left(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,Inv\,Fun}\left(t\right)\right) = t\).

\par\smallskip\noindent\emph{Proof of the main assertion.}\enspace
A descending chain would make the natural-number measure \(x \mapsto \operatorname{semilength}\left(x\right)\) strictly decrease at each step, so the relation is well-founded.
Proceed by well-founded induction to prove \(\forall p\, :\, \operatorname{Dyck\,Word},\; \operatorname{semilength}(p) = \operatorname{num\,Nodes}(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree}(p))\). For an arbitrary element we may assume the claim for each strictly smaller element.

\begin{proofstep}
Assume \(\neg \mathrm{False}\).
By definition, we obtain \(\operatorname{node}(\operatorname{unit},\allowbreak{} \operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(\operatorname{inside\,Part}(p)),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(\operatorname{outside\,Part}(p))) = \operatorname{node}(\operatorname{unit},\allowbreak{} \operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(\operatorname{inside\,Part}(p)),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(\operatorname{outside\,Part}(p)))\).
\end{proofstep}
By \paperlink{theorem:34}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:34}}, we obtain \(\operatorname{semilength}(\operatorname{inside\,Part}(p)) < \operatorname{semilength}(p)\).
By \paperlink{theorem:35}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:35}}, we obtain \(\operatorname{semilength}(\operatorname{outside\,Part}(p)) < \operatorname{semilength}(p)\).
Use the previously proved fact \(\operatorname{semilength}(\operatorname{inside\,Part}(p)) < \operatorname{semilength}(p)\).
Apply the induction hypothesis to \(\operatorname{inside\,Part}\left(p\right)\) to obtain \(\operatorname{semilength}(\operatorname{inside\,Part}(p)) = \operatorname{num\,Nodes}(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree}(\operatorname{inside\,Part}(p)))\).
Use the previously proved fact \(\operatorname{semilength}(\operatorname{outside\,Part}(p)) < \operatorname{semilength}(p)\).
Apply the induction hypothesis to \(\operatorname{outside\,Part}\left(p\right)\) to obtain \(\operatorname{semilength}(\operatorname{outside\,Part}(p)) = \operatorname{num\,Nodes}(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree}(\operatorname{outside\,Part}(p)))\).
By definition, we obtain \(\operatorname{num\,Nodes}(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree}(\operatorname{inside\,Part}(p))) + \operatorname{num\,Nodes}(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree}(\operatorname{outside\,Part}(p))) + 1 = \operatorname{num\,Nodes}(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(\operatorname{inside\,Part}(p))) + \operatorname{num\,Nodes}(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(\operatorname{outside\,Part}(p))) + 1\).
Rewriting with \(\operatorname{semilength}(\operatorname{outside\,Part}(p)) = \operatorname{num\,Nodes}(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree}(\operatorname{outside\,Part}(p)))\) in the preceding result gives \(\operatorname{num\,Nodes}(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree}(\operatorname{inside\,Part}(p))) + \operatorname{semilength}(\operatorname{outside\,Part}(p)) + 1 = \operatorname{num\,Nodes}(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(\operatorname{inside\,Part}(p))) + \operatorname{num\,Nodes}(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(\operatorname{outside\,Part}(p))) + 1\).
Rewriting with \(\operatorname{semilength}(\operatorname{inside\,Part}(p)) = \operatorname{num\,Nodes}(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree}(\operatorname{inside\,Part}(p)))\) in the preceding result gives \(\operatorname{semilength}(\operatorname{inside\,Part}(p)) + \operatorname{semilength}(\operatorname{outside\,Part}(p)) + 1 = \operatorname{num\,Nodes}(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(\operatorname{inside\,Part}(p))) + \operatorname{num\,Nodes}(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(\operatorname{outside\,Part}(p))) + 1\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{theorem:33}{Lemma~\ref{theorem:33}} (using \(\neg \left(p = 0\right)\)) in the preceding result gives \(\operatorname{semilength}(p) = \operatorname{num\,Nodes}(\operatorname{node}(\operatorname{unit},\allowbreak{} \operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(\operatorname{inside\,Part}(p)),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(\operatorname{outside\,Part}(p))))\).
By the preceding argument, we obtain \(\operatorname{semilength}(p) = \operatorname{num\,Nodes}(\begin{cases}\operatorname{Tree\mathord{:}nil} &\text{if } \mathrm{False}\\ \operatorname{node}(\operatorname{unit},\allowbreak{} \operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(\operatorname{inside\,Part}(p)),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(\operatorname{outside\,Part}(p))) &\text{if } \neg \mathrm{False}\end{cases})\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:646974655f636f6e6772}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:646974655f636f6e6772}}, \paperlink{premise:65715f66616c7365}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:65715f66616c7365}} (using \(\neg \left(p = 0\right)\)) and the two identities established above in the preceding result gives \(\operatorname{semilength}(p) = \operatorname{num\,Nodes}(\begin{cases}\operatorname{Tree\mathord{:}nil} &\text{if } p = 0\\ \operatorname{node}(\operatorname{unit},\allowbreak{} \operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(\operatorname{inside\,Part}(p)),\allowbreak{} \operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(\operatorname{outside\,Part}(p))) &\text{if } \neg (p = 0)\end{cases})\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:646974655f636f6e6772}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:646974655f636f6e6772}} and the two identities established above in the preceding result gives the same displayed equality.
Rewriting with \paperlink{defeq:15}{defining equation~D\ref{defeq:15}} in the preceding result gives \(\operatorname{semilength}(p) = \operatorname{num\,Nodes}(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun}(p))\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:45717569762e636f655f666e5f6d6b}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:45717569762e636f655f666e5f6d6b}}, \paperlink{aux:43:1}{Auxiliary lemma~43.1} and \paperlink{aux:43:2}{Auxiliary lemma~43.2} in the preceding result gives \(\operatorname{semilength}(p) = \operatorname{num\,Nodes}(\operatorname{Equiv\mathord{:}mk}(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,To\,Fun},\allowbreak{} \operatorname{equiv\,Tree\,Inv\,Fun})(p))\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{defeq:18}{defining equation~D\ref{defeq:18}} in the preceding result gives \(\operatorname{semilength}(p) = \operatorname{num\,Nodes}(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree}(p))\).
\end{proofstep}
The proposition or its negation holds. Hence \(\operatorname{semilength}(p) = \operatorname{num\,Nodes}(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree}(p))\).
\end{proofstep}
The induction gives \(\forall p\, :\, \operatorname{Dyck\,Word},\; \operatorname{semilength}(p) = \operatorname{num\,Nodes}(\operatorname{equiv\,Tree}(p))\).
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[{The Catalan count for Dyck words of fixed semilength}]\label{theorem:44}
Let \(n\) be a natural number. Then
\begin{center}
\(\displaystyle |\{p\in \operatorname{Dyck\,Word} \mid \operatorname{semilength}(p) = n\}| = \operatorname{catalan}(n).\)
\end{center}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
By \paperlink{premise:46696e747970652e636172645f636f65}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:46696e747970652e636172645f636f65}} with \(\alpha = \operatorname{Tree}\left(\operatorname{Unit}\right)\) and \(s = \operatorname{trees\,Of\,Num\,Nodes\,Eq}\left(n\right)\), we obtain \(|\operatorname{trees\,Of\,Num\,Nodes\,Eq}(n)| = |\operatorname{trees\,Of\,Num\,Nodes\,Eq}(n)|\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:65715f6f665f686571}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:65715f6f665f686571}}, \paperlink{premise:46696e747970652e636172645f636f6e677227}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:46696e747970652e636172645f636f6e677227}} and substitution of equals in the preceding result gives the same displayed equality.
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:547265652e74726565734f664e756d4e6f64657345715f636172645f65715f636174616c616e}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:547265652e74726565734f664e756d4e6f64657345715f636172645f65715f636174616c616e}} in the preceding result gives \(\left|\operatorname{trees\,Of\,Num\,Nodes\,Eq}\left(n\right)\right| = \operatorname{catalan}\left(n\right)\).
Rewriting with \paperlink{premise:46696e747970652e6f6645717569765f63617264}{Prerequisite~P\ref{premise:46696e747970652e6f6645717569765f63617264}} in the preceding result gives \(|\{p\in \operatorname{Dyck\,Word} \mid \operatorname{semilength}(p) = n\}| = \operatorname{catalan}(n)\).
\end{proof}
